vorfahrt-01.question: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, two vehicles approach at the same time. Who has right of way?

options.a: The faster vehicle
options.b: The vehicle coming from the right
options.c: The larger vehicle
options.d: Whoever honks first

vorfahrt-01.explanation: Without signs stating otherwise, the basic rule 'right before left' applies.

vorfahrt-02.question: You see a downward-pointing triangular sign with a red border (Zeichen 205). What does it mean?

options.a: Priority road
options.b: No entry
options.c: Yield / give way
options.d: Stop

vorfahrt-02.explanation: Zeichen 205 requires yielding right of way, but not a full stop, as long as visibility is sufficient.

vorfahrt-03.question: At an octagonal red 'STOP' sign (Zeichen 206), you must...

options.a: always come to a complete stop, even if no other vehicle is visible
options.b: stop only if another vehicle is approaching
options.c: only slow down
options.d: only stop at night

vorfahrt-03.explanation: The stop sign always requires a complete stop, regardless of other traffic.

vorfahrt-04.question: The yellow diamond-shaped sign with a white border (Zeichen 301) indicates that...

options.a: the road ends
options.b: you have right of way at this point
options.c: a roundabout follows
options.d: pedestrians have priority

vorfahrt-04.explanation: Zeichen 301 marks priority at that single point relative to the crossing road.

vorfahrt-05.question: The rectangular yellow sign with a white border, which can also show the road's curves (Zeichen 306), means:

options.a: Priority road - right of way continues along the entire marked route
options.b: End of motorway
options.c: No motor vehicles
options.d: Pedestrian zone

vorfahrt-05.explanation: Unlike Zeichen 301, Zeichen 306 applies continuously along the entire priority road until Zeichen 307 ends it.

vorfahrt-06.question: How do you behave when entering a roundabout (Zeichen 215), unless signs state otherwise?

options.a: Vehicles entering the roundabout have priority
options.b: Vehicles already in the roundabout have priority
options.c: Right before left applies
options.d: Whoever is faster goes first

vorfahrt-06.explanation: In a roundabout, traffic already circulating generally has priority over vehicles entering.

vorfahrt-07.question: You want to turn left at an unsignalled intersection. Oncoming traffic is going straight. Who has right of way?

options.a: You, because you arrived at the intersection first
options.b: Neither, both must wait
options.c: The oncoming traffic going straight
options.d: The vehicle turning left, if it signals

vorfahrt-07.explanation: A vehicle turning left must let oncoming traffic going straight or turning right pass first.

vorfahrt-08.question: Two vehicles from opposite directions both want to turn left at the same intersection at the same time. How do they usually proceed?

options.a: They pass each other 'curve before curve', right side to right side
options.b: The one on the left always has to wait
options.c: Both must stop completely and negotiate
options.d: The one on the right always has to wait

vorfahrt-08.explanation: When both turn left simultaneously, they normally pass each other right side to right side (curve before curve).

vorfahrt-09.question: A tram is approaching from a side street on your right. How do you behave if no sign states otherwise?

options.a: You have right of way because the tram is coming from a minor road
options.b: The tram generally has right of way
options.c: Right before left applies just like for cars
options.d: Right of way is decided randomly

vorfahrt-09.explanation: Rail vehicles generally have right of way, regardless of the direction they come from.

vorfahrt-10.question: A lane ends and traffic must merge. How does the 'zip merge' (Reißverschlussverfahren) work?

options.a: Whoever gets there first goes first
options.b: The left lane always has priority
options.c: Vehicles from both lanes take turns merging one after another
options.d: Only trucks are allowed to merge

vorfahrt-10.explanation: Just before the lane narrows, vehicles from the ending lane are let in one at a time, alternating.

vorfahrt-11.question: You are driving from a clearly recognizable field/dirt track onto a normal road. A vehicle is approaching from the right on the road. Who has right of way?

options.a: You, because 'right before left' only applies between roads of equal importance
options.b: The vehicle on the road; the field track counts as a minor road
options.c: Right before left applies without restriction
options.d: Both must stop at the same time

vorfahrt-11.explanation: Clearly minor routes (field tracks, driveways) have no right of way even without a sign.

vorfahrt-12.question: You are driving from a driveway onto the road. What rule applies?

options.a: You must behave as if coming from a minor road and have no right of way
options.b: Right before left applies normally
options.c: You always have priority over moving traffic
options.d: You only have to wait during daylight

vorfahrt-12.explanation: Anyone entering traffic from a driveway, parking space, or similar must proceed with special caution and has no right of way.

vorfahrt-13.question: A police officer gives hand signals at an intersection that contradict the traffic light. What applies?

options.a: The traffic light always takes precedence
options.b: The officer's signals take precedence over traffic lights and signs
options.c: You may choose which one to follow
options.d: Both regulations apply simultaneously

vorfahrt-13.explanation: Signals and instructions from police officers always take precedence over traffic lights and signs.

vorfahrt-14.question: At a traffic light with a green arrow sign allowing right turns on red (Zeichen 720), you may turn right on red. What must you still do?

options.a: Nothing, you may proceed without stopping
options.b: Only honk as a warning
options.c: Stop first and yield to other traffic and pedestrians
options.d: Only stop at night

vorfahrt-14.explanation: The green arrow only allows a right turn on red after coming to a full stop and if no one is endangered.

vorfahrt-15.question: You are approaching a pedestrian crossing (zebra crossing, Zeichen 293). A pedestrian wants to cross the road. How do you behave?

options.a: You must wait and allow the pedestrian to cross
options.b: The pedestrian must wait until you have passed
options.c: You only need to stop at a red light
options.d: Right before left applies

vorfahrt-15.explanation: At a zebra crossing, pedestrians who clearly intend to cross have priority.

vorfahrt-16.question: At an intersection, the traffic light has completely failed due to a power outage and there are no other signs. What applies?

options.a: Right before left
options.b: The intersection may not be entered at all
options.c: First to arrive goes first
options.d: A priority road automatically applies

vorfahrt-16.explanation: If the traffic light fails and no other regulation applies, the basic right-before-left rule takes over.

vorfahrt-17.question: You are turning right, and a cyclist is going straight on a mandatory cycle path next to you. Who has priority?

options.a: You, because you have already positioned yourself to turn
options.b: The cyclist going straight
options.c: It is negotiated with hand signals
options.d: The cyclist must always dismount

vorfahrt-17.explanation: When turning, priority must be given to cyclists and pedestrians going straight; when in doubt, proceed at walking pace.

vorfahrt-18.question: You have already positioned yourself to turn and switched on the indicator. What applies regarding right of way?

options.a: Your right of way automatically ends
options.b: Your right of way continues unchanged until you have turned
options.c: You must wait in every case
options.d: The indicator automatically grants you right of way

vorfahrt-18.explanation: Positioning and signalling do not change an existing right of way.

vorfahrt-19.question: An emergency vehicle with blue lights and siren approaches from behind. What must you do, even if you would normally have right of way?

options.a: Immediately clear a path, if necessary by forming an emergency corridor or pulling over
options.b: Continue driving normally, since you have right of way
options.c: Accelerate to reach the intersection first
options.d: Only honk in response

vorfahrt-19.explanation: The special rights of emergency vehicles with blue lights and siren override every other right-of-way rule.

vorfahrt-20.question: A triangular sign with a red border shows a cross symbol (Zeichen 102, 'intersection'). What does it mean?

options.a: It re-regulates right of way at this intersection
options.b: It merely warns of an upcoming intersection; right before left still applies
options.c: It indicates a priority road
options.d: It prohibits crossing

vorfahrt-20.explanation: Warning signs like 102 only warn; they do not change the applicable right-of-way rule.

vorfahrt-21.question: A priority road (Zeichen 306) crosses a railway crossing without a barrier. A train is approaching. Who has priority?

options.a: The priority road, since it is protected by Zeichen 306
options.b: The train always has priority regardless of road signage
options.c: Right before left decides
options.d: Whoever arrives first

vorfahrt-21.explanation: Trains at level crossings always have priority over road traffic, regardless of other signage.

vorfahrt-22.question: A road is divided by a central island and crosses a road of equal rank with no signs. How does right of way apply?

options.a: Right before left applies uniformly to the whole road, regardless of the island
options.b: Each half of the carriageway has its own right-of-way rule
options.c: The central island cancels any right-of-way rule
options.d: A priority road automatically applies

vorfahrt-22.explanation: A structural division by a central island does not change the road's basic right-of-way rule.

vorfahrt-23.question: You come out of a one-way street with no priority signs and meet a road of equal rank. What rule applies?

options.a: The one-way street automatically has priority
options.b: Right before left applies as at any other intersection of equal-ranking roads
options.c: Oncoming traffic always has priority
options.d: There is no right-of-way rule in one-way streets

vorfahrt-23.explanation: A one-way street is a perfectly normal road for right-of-way purposes; without signs, right before left applies.

vorfahrt-24.question: There is an obstacle on your side of the road (e.g. parked vehicles), forcing you onto the opposite lane. What applies, regardless of right-before-left?

options.a: You must give way to oncoming traffic and must not obstruct it
options.b: You automatically have priority because the obstacle forces you to swerve
options.c: Oncoming traffic must stop and wait
options.d: Right before left applies as at an intersection

vorfahrt-24.explanation: Anyone who must use the opposite lane because of an obstacle must give way to oncoming traffic.

vorfahrt-25.question: A sign like Zeichen 306 but crossed out in grey/black (Zeichen 307) means:

options.a: Start of a new priority road
options.b: No entry into the road
options.c: End of the priority road
options.d: End of the motorway

vorfahrt-25.explanation: Zeichen 307 cancels the continuous right of way established by Zeichen 306.

zeichen-01.question: A white round sign with a red border and a black number (e.g. '50') indicates:

options.a: Recommended minimum speed
options.b: Maximum permitted speed in km/h
options.c: Distance to the next town in km
options.d: Permitted parking duration in minutes

zeichen-01.explanation: Zeichen 274 sets the maximum permitted speed, which must not be exceeded.

zeichen-02.question: The same sign as the speed limit but crossed out in grey (Zeichen 278) means:

options.a: End of the previously ordered speed limit
options.b: Additional speed limit in wet conditions
options.c: End of the overtaking ban
options.d: Start of a speed limit

zeichen-02.explanation: A crossed-out sign cancels the previously applicable order.

zeichen-03.question: A round red sign with a white horizontal bar (Zeichen 267) means:

options.a: Stop, give way
options.b: Free passage for all vehicles
options.c: No entry for vehicles of any kind
options.d: One-way street in the direction of travel

zeichen-03.explanation: Zeichen 267 prohibits entry in that direction, typically at the end of a one-way street.

zeichen-04.question: A triangular warning sign showing playing children (Zeichen 136) warns of:

options.a: A school where no special caution is needed
options.b: Children possibly suddenly appearing on the road
options.c: A ban on playgrounds
options.d: A mandatory 30 km/h speed limit

zeichen-04.explanation: The sign warns of children near the road, e.g. near schools or playgrounds; increased caution and readiness to brake are required.

zeichen-05.question: A triangular sign with a red border and an exclamation mark (Zeichen 101) generally means:

options.a: General danger spot - increased attention required
options.b: Prohibition of all vehicles
options.c: Priority road begins
options.d: End of all prohibitions

zeichen-05.explanation: This sign is often combined with an additional plate specifying the concrete danger.

zeichen-06.question: A triangular sign shows a narrowing road (Zeichen 120/121). You should:

options.a: Accelerate to pass the narrow section quickly
options.b: Ignore it if no oncoming traffic is visible
options.c: Adjust speed and merge into the correct lane in good time
options.d: Stop on the hard shoulder

zeichen-06.explanation: At road narrowings, merging early with foresight and adjusting speed is important.

zeichen-07.question: A triangular warning sign with a train symbol (e.g. Zeichen 151) announces:

options.a: A subway station nearby
options.b: A level crossing without full or half barriers
options.c: A tram stop
options.d: A railway museum

zeichen-07.explanation: Such signs announce level crossings without barriers, where special caution is required.

zeichen-08.question: A white sign with a red St. Andrew's cross (Zeichen 201) at a single-track level crossing means:

options.a: You must always stop if a rail vehicle is approaching
options.b: It is merely a decorative marking
options.c: The road has priority over the railway
options.d: The rail line is out of service

zeichen-08.explanation: The St. Andrew's cross marks a level crossing; you must stop if a train is approaching.

zeichen-09.question: A round white sign with a red border and no further symbols (Zeichen 250) means:

options.a: Prohibition for motorcycles only
options.b: Prohibition for vehicles of any kind
options.c: End of all prohibitions
options.d: Priority for pedestrians

zeichen-09.explanation: Zeichen 250 closes the route to all types of vehicles, with a few statutory exceptions.

zeichen-10.question: A round white sign with a red border showing a car and a motorcycle (Zeichen 260) means:

options.a: Prohibition for motor vehicles
options.b: Only motor vehicles allowed
options.c: No parking for motor vehicles
options.d: Petrol station nearby

zeichen-10.explanation: Zeichen 260 prohibits motorized vehicles from passing (with defined exceptions, e.g. mopeds under certain conditions).

zeichen-11.question: A round blue sign with a white bicycle symbol (Zeichen 237) means:

options.a: Bicycles are prohibited here
options.b: Cycle path with mandatory use for cyclists
options.c: Bicycle rental nearby
options.d: Bicycle repair workshop

zeichen-11.explanation: If a cycle path is marked with Zeichen 237, cyclists must use it, provided it is safe to use.

zeichen-12.question: A round blue sign with a pedestrian symbol above a bicycle symbol (Zeichen 240) means:

options.a: Separate cycle and footpath
options.b: Pedestrians prohibited
options.c: Shared pedestrian and cycle path
options.d: Bicycles prohibited on the footpath

zeichen-12.explanation: On a shared pedestrian and cycle path, pedestrians and cyclists must share the space and show mutual consideration.

zeichen-13.question: A blue rectangular sign with a white arrow pointing up, marking a one-way street (Zeichen 220) means:

options.a: The road may only be driven in the direction of the arrow
options.b: The road is open in all directions
options.c: The road is closed
options.d: Only pedestrians may use the road

zeichen-13.explanation: On a one-way street, driving is only permitted in the direction indicated by the arrow.

zeichen-14.question: A blue sign with a stylised motorway bridge symbol (Zeichen 330.1) indicates:

options.a: End of the motorway
options.b: Start of the motorway
options.c: Rest area in 500 m
options.d: Roadworks on the motorway

zeichen-14.explanation: From this sign onward, special motorway rules apply, e.g. prohibition of pedestrians and slow vehicles.

zeichen-15.question: The same symbol as the motorway start, but crossed out in grey (Zeichen 330.2), indicates:

options.a: End of the motorway
options.b: Additional motorway entrance
options.c: Motorway interchange coming up
options.d: Increased speed limit

zeichen-15.explanation: From this sign onward, normal road traffic rules apply again.

zeichen-16.question: A blue round sign with a red border and a red diagonal cross (Zeichen 283) means:

options.a: Restricted no-stopping zone
options.b: Absolute no-stopping zone
options.c: Parking allowed
options.d: Loading zone

zeichen-16.explanation: In an absolute no-stopping zone, stopping is never permitted, not even briefly to let someone in or out.

zeichen-17.question: A blue round sign with a red border and a single red diagonal stripe (Zeichen 286) means:

options.a: Restricted no-stopping zone - brief stopping to load or unload is allowed
options.b: Absolute no-stopping zone with no exceptions
options.c: Parking only with a parking ticket
options.d: Priority road

zeichen-17.explanation: In a restricted no-stopping zone, brief stopping is allowed but not parking (leaving the vehicle for more than 3 minutes).

zeichen-18.question: A blue square sign with a white 'P' (Zeichen 314) means:

options.a: Parking prohibited
options.b: Petrol station
options.c: Parking allowed
options.d: Car park full

zeichen-18.explanation: Zeichen 314 marks an area where parking is explicitly allowed.

zeichen-19.question: A blue sign with a 'P' and a symbol showing partial parking on the pavement (Zeichen 315) means:

options.a: Parking on the pavement is generally prohibited
options.b: Parking is allowed partly or fully on the pavement, depending on the sub-symbol
options.c: Only bicycles may be parked there
options.d: The pavement is closed to pedestrians

zeichen-19.explanation: The exact type of permitted pavement parking (full, half, perpendicular) is defined by the specific symbol.

zeichen-20.question: A triangular warning sign showing a person with a shovel (Zeichen 123) announces:

options.a: A road works / construction site
options.b: An agricultural area
options.c: A playground
options.d: A landfill site

zeichen-20.explanation: The sign warns of a work site; increased attention and reduced speed are appropriate.

zeichen-21.question: A blue square sign with a white triangle showing a person crossing (Zeichen 350) marks:

options.a: A bus stop
options.b: A pedestrian crossing
options.c: A pedestrian zone
options.d: An overtaking ban for pedestrians

zeichen-21.explanation: This sign, together with the zebra-stripe road markings, indicates a pedestrian crossing.

zeichen-22.question: A round white sign with five diagonal black stripes (Zeichen 282) means:

options.a: End of all previously ordered restrictions on that stretch of road
options.b: Start of an overtaking ban
options.c: End of roadworks
options.d: Increased right of way

zeichen-22.explanation: Zeichen 282 collectively cancels all previously applicable stretch-related prohibitions and restrictions.

zeichen-23.question: A round white sign with a red border showing two cars, one black and one red (Zeichen 276), means:

options.a: Right of way over oncoming traffic
options.b: Mandatory convoy driving
options.c: No overtaking for motor vehicles
options.d: No entry for two vehicles at once

zeichen-23.explanation: Zeichen 276 prohibits overtaking motor vehicles; the prohibition usually ends with Zeichen 280.

zeichen-24.question: A round blue sign with a white arrow pointing right (Zeichen 209) means:

options.a: Recommendation to go right
options.b: Mandatory direction of travel to the right
options.c: Turning right prohibited
options.d: Passing obstacles on the right is allowed

zeichen-24.explanation: Mandatory direction arrows (Zeichen 209 ff.) require driving in the indicated direction.

zeichen-25.question: Below a traffic sign there is a small white rectangle with additional text or a symbol. What is that?

options.a: An additional plate that specifies the scope or meaning of the main sign
options.b: A purely decorative element with no legal meaning
options.c: An advertisement
options.d: A reference to a petrol station

zeichen-25.explanation: Additional plates can specify, for example, validity times, distances, or exceptions for certain vehicle types.

gefahr-01.question: You are driving on the motorway in the rain. How does the braking distance change compared to a dry road?

options.a: It stays almost the same, only steering gets heavier
options.b: It becomes clearly longer because the tyres grip less
options.c: It becomes shorter because water cools the brakes
options.d: It only changes above 150 km/h

gefahr-01.explanation: A wet road reduces friction between tyre and surface. The car needs more distance to stop, so you must increase your following distance.

gefahr-02.question: What is aquaplaning?

options.a: Tyre damage caused by too little air pressure
options.b: A braking fault that happens in wet weather
options.c: A film of water lifts the tyres off the road
options.d: Engine damage caused by water getting inside

gefahr-02.explanation: With a lot of water on the road and high speed, a wedge of water can form and separate the tyre from the asphalt. The car then loses contact with the road and becomes hard to steer or brake.

gefahr-03.question: How should you react during aquaplaning?

options.a: Ease off the accelerator, keep the wheel straight, don't brake hard
options.b: Brake fully at once so the wheels grip again
options.c: Steer strongly against it to hold your lane
options.d: Accelerate to get through the puddle faster

gefahr-03.explanation: As long as the tyres have no contact with the road, steering and braking barely work. You should release the accelerator, roll straight ahead calmly, and wait until the tyres grip again.

gefahr-04.question: In winter, where does black ice form especially fast, even while the rest of the road is still dry?

options.a: In the middle of wide main roads
options.b: On bridges and in the shade of trees
options.c: Only on motorways
options.d: Only right before traffic lights

gefahr-04.explanation: Bridges cool down from both above and below, so they freeze first. Shaded spots get less sun and stay cold and damp longer. The risk there is especially high.

gefahr-05.question: You are driving at 80 km/h. Roughly how long is your reaction distance before you even start braking?

options.a: About 8 metres
options.b: About 16 metres
options.c: About 24 metres
options.d: About 40 metres

gefahr-05.explanation: A simple rule of thumb: divide the speed in km/h by 10, then multiply by 3, to get the reaction distance in metres. At 80 km/h that is roughly 24 metres.

gefahr-06.question: What does the 'half your speedometer reading' rule of thumb mean for following distance on the motorway?

options.a: The distance in metres should be at least half your speed in km/h
options.b: You should only drive at half the allowed speed
options.c: The distance may be at most half a vehicle length
options.d: You should take a break after half the route

gefahr-06.explanation: At 100 km/h that would be at least 50 metres of distance. This rule of thumb is easy to remember but does not replace a more careful calculation in poor conditions.

gefahr-07.question: How does the 'three-second rule' for checking following distance work?

options.a: You count three seconds before pulling away
options.b: You pick a fixed point and count how many seconds pass before your own car reaches it
options.c: You hold the horn for three seconds when there is danger
options.d: You wait three seconds after braking before driving on

gefahr-07.explanation: When the vehicle ahead passes a point, you start counting. If you reach that point before three seconds pass, your distance is too short.

gefahr-08.question: You see a ball roll onto the road from the roadside. How should you react?

options.a: Keep driving normally, a ball is not an obstacle
options.b: Slow down at once and expect a child to run after the ball
options.c: Just sound the horn and keep driving normally
options.d: Speed up to get past the spot quickly

gefahr-08.explanation: A rolling ball is a classic warning sign that a child may run onto the road right after it without looking. Slowing down carefully and being ready to brake is important here.

gefahr-09.question: A bus stops at a bus stop and signals with its indicator. What must you do as the driver of another vehicle?

options.a: Adjust your speed so the bus can pull out again if needed
options.b: Overtake quickly before the bus moves off
options.c: Just sound the horn to warn the bus driver
options.d: Nothing, the bus has to wait for a gap itself

gefahr-09.explanation: When a bus at a stop signals, you must let it pull back into traffic and, if necessary, reduce your own speed.

gefahr-10.question: Why is the 'blind spot' dangerous when changing lanes?

options.a: It only affects motorcycles
options.b: It only exists in the dark
options.c: A vehicle beside you can be invisible in both the mirrors
options.d: It only occurs in rain

gefahr-10.explanation: There is an area beside and slightly behind the car that neither the interior nor the side mirrors show. That is why you should also glance over your shoulder before changing lanes.

gefahr-11.question: You are driving at night in fog. What is the correct behaviour?

options.a: Turn on full beam so you can see further
options.b: Reduce speed significantly and use dipped headlights or fog lights
options.c: Leave the hazard lights on permanently and keep driving normally
options.d: Follow as closely as possible so you can see the tail lights

gefahr-11.explanation: Full beam reflects off the water droplets in fog and actually worsens visibility. Dipped headlights or fog lights along with reduced speed are correct.

gefahr-12.question: According to the rule, rear fog lights may only be used when visibility is reduced to below how far?

options.a: Below 50 metres
options.b: Below 500 metres
options.c: Below 5 metres
options.d: Always in any fog, no matter how light

gefahr-12.explanation: Rear fog lights are very bright and dazzle others when visibility is better. They may only be switched on once visibility drops below 50 metres.

gefahr-13.question: Why is microsleep at the wheel especially dangerous?

options.a: You notice in time that you are falling asleep and can stop beforehand
options.b: It only happens on hours-long night drives, never during the day
options.c: You lose control completely for a few seconds without noticing in time
options.d: It usually lasts several minutes, leaving enough time to react in time

gefahr-13.explanation: Even a few seconds of microsleep at motorway speed are enough to drift far off your lane. That is why tiredness must be taken seriously, with breaks taken in good time.

gefahr-14.question: How does alcohol in the blood typically affect driving behaviour?

options.a: It improves concentration but slightly slows reaction time
options.b: It lengthens reaction time and leads to overestimating one's own ability
options.c: It only affects night vision
options.d: It has no effect at all below 0.5 per mille

gefahr-14.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol impair reaction time and judgement. Many affected drivers rate themselves as less impaired than they actually are.

gefahr-15.question: You are driving into low sun that is dazzling you badly. What is correct?

options.a: Use the sun visor, reduce speed, and stop if you can no longer see anything
options.b: Open the window so you can see better
options.c: Close your eyes briefly until the glare passes
options.d: Turn on full beam to increase contrast

gefahr-15.explanation: In strong glare from low sun, obstacles or pedestrians are often seen too late. You must adjust your speed and, in extreme cases, stop in a safe spot.

gefahr-16.question: Why are vehicles parked at the roadside a typical source of danger?

options.a: Only illegally parked vehicles pose a danger, correctly parked ones do not
options.b: Children or pedestrians can suddenly step out from behind them
options.c: The danger only exists in the dark; in daylight you see in time
options.d: At walking pace there is no longer any danger at all

gefahr-16.explanation: Parked cars block the view of the pavement. A child or pedestrian can be hidden behind them and suddenly step onto the road.

gefahr-17.question: You drive past a wooded area and see a sign showing a leaping animal. What should you do?

options.a: Speed up to get through the danger zone quickly
options.b: Only slow down if it is dark
options.c: Reduce speed and watch the edges of the road closely
options.d: Ignore it, the sign only applies to motorcyclists

gefahr-17.explanation: The animal crossing sign warns that animals may suddenly run out of the woods onto the road. Slowing down and watching the roadside closely reduces the risk.

gefahr-18.question: What generally happens to the braking distance if speed doubles?

options.a: It becomes roughly four times as long
options.b: It becomes roughly twice as long
options.c: It stays almost the same
options.d: It only becomes about ten percent longer

gefahr-18.explanation: The pure braking distance grows with the square of the speed. Double the speed roughly means four times the braking distance.

gefahr-19.question: Why should you keep more distance than usual when following a truck in a line of traffic?

options.a: Because trucks brake more easily than cars
options.b: Because the view ahead is blocked and hazards are seen later
options.c: Because trucks have no brake lights
options.d: Because keeping less than 100 metres is illegal there

gefahr-19.explanation: Behind a large vehicle you can barely see the traffic situation further ahead. More distance gives you extra time to react to sudden braking.

gefahr-20.question: A child is standing alone at the edge of the road and is not looking in your direction. How do you behave?

options.a: Pass with enough side clearance and keep your speed, that is enough of a safety margin
options.b: Sound the horn so the child steps aside in time, and keep your speed
options.c: Just check that you are within the speed limit, no extra caution is needed
options.d: Reduce speed and be ready to brake, since children can react unpredictably

gefahr-20.explanation: Children often cannot yet properly judge the danger they are in around traffic and may suddenly run. Drivers must therefore be especially careful and ready to brake near children.

gefahr-21.question: How does severe tiredness affect fitness to drive compared with mild alcohol consumption?

options.a: Tiredness has no effect on driving at all
options.b: Tiredness only affects eyesight, not reaction time
options.c: Severe tiredness can impair reaction ability similarly to alcohol
options.d: Tiredness only affects professional drivers

gefahr-21.explanation: Studies show that severe tiredness can worsen reaction time and attention about as much as an elevated blood alcohol level. Breaks when tired are therefore very important.

gefahr-22.question: You approach a tram stop where passengers are getting off. What must you keep in mind?

options.a: You may pass the tram without any restriction
options.b: You must drive especially slowly and let pedestrians cross to the stop safely
options.c: You must always wait behind the tram until it is completely empty
options.d: The rule only applies to cyclists

gefahr-22.explanation: Passengers getting off a tram often have to cross the road to reach the pavement. Vehicles must therefore pass especially slowly and carefully.

gefahr-23.question: Why is a road covered with wet autumn leaves especially dangerous?

options.a: Wet leaves can reduce the friction between tyre and road almost as much as ice, especially when braking or cornering
options.b: Leaves only reduce visibility of the road surface, grip stays unchanged
options.c: Leaves are only dangerous for cyclists, not for cars
options.d: Both dry and wet leaves actually improve grip because they act like a mat

gefahr-23.explanation: Wet leaves form a slippery film on the asphalt and can reduce friction almost as much as ice. This can quickly lead to skidding, especially when braking or cornering.

gefahr-24.question: Why are cyclists especially at risk in a truck's blind spot when it turns?

options.a: The truck driver simply cannot see them in certain areas beside and in front of the vehicle
options.b: Cyclists there are always riding too fast
options.c: Trucks have no mirrors
options.d: The problem only affects bicycles without lights

gefahr-24.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots where a cyclist cannot be seen even with mirrors. This repeatedly causes accidents, especially when turning right.

gefahr-25.question: You drive through a puddle that is deeper than it looks. What can happen?

options.a: Nothing, deep puddles are harmless for cars
options.b: The steering can suddenly pull hard and the car can drift off its lane
options.c: The car automatically slows down
options.d: Only the windows can fog up

gefahr-25.explanation: Uneven water resistance on the two sides of the car can suddenly pull it sideways. You should drive through deep puddles slowly and hold the wheel firmly.

umwelt-01.question: Which driving style saves the most fuel?

options.a: Constant hard acceleration and braking
options.b: Always driving in the lowest gear
options.c: Driving with foresight and shifting to a higher gear early
options.d: Letting the engine idle longer at every stop

umwelt-01.explanation: Anticipating traffic and avoiding heavy braking and acceleration clearly reduces fuel use. Shifting up early keeps the engine speed low and saves even more.

umwelt-02.question: What is the minimum legal tread depth for a car tyre?

options.a: 0.4 millimetres
options.b: 1.6 millimetres
options.c: 4 millimetres
options.d: 8 millimetres

umwelt-02.explanation: The legal minimum tread depth is 1.6 millimetres. For good safety in wet conditions, a much higher value is often recommended.

umwelt-03.question: What effect does too-low tyre pressure have on fuel use and safety?

options.a: Fuel use rises and braking distance can get longer
options.b: Fuel use drops but braking distance gets longer
options.c: Both stay unchanged
options.d: The tyre lasts longer as a result

umwelt-03.explanation: Tyre pressure that is too low increases rolling resistance, which raises fuel use, and also worsens handling. Checking tyre pressure regularly is therefore worthwhile.

umwelt-04.question: What does an ABS (anti-lock braking system) do?

options.a: It automatically shortens every braking distance to a minimum
options.b: It only works at speeds above 30 km/h
options.c: It completely prevents the vehicle from sliding on black ice
options.d: It stops the wheels locking under hard braking, so you stay able to steer

umwelt-04.explanation: ABS prevents the wheels from locking under hard braking. This keeps the vehicle steerable, even though the braking distance itself is not necessarily shortened by it.

umwelt-05.question: What does an ESP system (electronic stability programme) do?

options.a: It automatically limits top speed in bad weather
options.b: It brakes individual wheels selectively to stop the vehicle from skidding
options.c: It automatically steers the wheel through corners
options.d: It only warns of low tyre pressure

umwelt-05.explanation: ESP detects when the vehicle is about to slide off its intended path and selectively brakes individual wheels to stabilise it.

umwelt-06.question: Why must the seatbelt be worn even on short trips?

options.a: Only because of the fine, a short trip itself is not dangerous
options.b: Even at low speed, accidents can cause serious injury; the belt holds the person back
options.c: The belt is not necessary on short trips because the car goes slower
options.d: The belt is only required for passengers

umwelt-06.explanation: Even at low speed, sudden braking or collisions can cause serious injury. The belt spreads the force and prevents you from being thrown forward.

umwelt-07.question: What is the purpose of an airbag in a car?

options.a: It completely replaces the seatbelt
options.b: It deploys in every impact, however minor, no matter how light
options.c: It cushions the impact on head and upper body in addition to the belt
options.d: It only protects the driver, not the passengers

umwelt-07.explanation: The airbag deploys during a strong impact and cushions the blow to the head and upper body. It does not replace the belt, but complements it.

umwelt-08.question: How do you recognize a genuine winter tyre as opposed to a pure summer tyre?

options.a: By the Alpine symbol (a mountain with a snowflake) on the tyre sidewall
options.b: By the M+S marking alone, regardless of when the tyre was made
options.c: By especially wide tyres, since wide tyres are automatically winter tyres
options.d: By the fact that it is sold as an 'all-season tyre'

umwelt-08.explanation: The Alpine symbol shows that a tyre meets the requirements for winter suitability. Since a transition period ended, the older M+S marking alone is no longer sufficient for newly manufactured tyres.

umwelt-09.question: What is the purpose of the periodic technical inspection (HU) at a testing organisation?

options.a: It only checks the vehicle's exhaust emissions
options.b: It checks the vehicle's road safety and technical condition
options.c: It is only necessary for new vehicles
options.d: If the vehicle passes the HU, no repairs are needed until the next inspection

umwelt-09.explanation: During the periodic inspection, brakes, steering, lights and emissions are checked, among other things, to ensure the vehicle meets road safety and environmental requirements.

umwelt-10.question: Which action lowers fuel consumption if you are stuck in traffic for more than a minute?

options.a: Stay idling, that barely uses more fuel than switching off and restarting
options.b: Switch off the engine at every stop, however short, even for just one or two seconds
options.c: Switch off the engine when the stop is expected to last a while
options.d: Keep the ventilation and air conditioning running, that saves more fuel than switching off the engine

umwelt-10.explanation: During longer stops, switching off the engine saves fuel and reduces emissions. Many modern cars do this automatically via a start-stop system.

umwelt-11.question: How does unnecessary weight in the car, such as unused luggage in the boot, affect fuel consumption?

options.a: More weight noticeably increases fuel consumption
options.b: Weight has no effect on consumption at all
options.c: More weight lowers consumption because the car drives more steadily
options.d: Weight only affects the brakes, not consumption

umwelt-11.explanation: The heavier the vehicle, the more energy it needs to accelerate. Unnecessary extra weight should therefore be removed to save fuel.

umwelt-12.question: Why should you remove a roof rack when it is not needed?

options.a: Because it adds so much weight that this affects consumption more than air resistance does
options.b: Because it worsens braking performance in wet conditions
options.c: Because it blocks the view of the rear mirror
options.d: Because it increases air resistance, which raises fuel consumption

umwelt-12.explanation: A mounted roof rack noticeably increases air resistance, especially at higher speed. This leads to clearly higher fuel consumption, even when nothing is loaded on it.

umwelt-13.question: Which owner's duty relates to regular vehicle maintenance?

options.a: The owner only has to bring the vehicle to the periodic inspection once a year, nothing more is required
options.b: The owner must ensure the vehicle stays roadworthy, for example through timely maintenance
options.c: Only the manufacturer is responsible for maintenance
options.d: Maintenance is voluntary and has no legal basis

umwelt-13.explanation: The keeper of a vehicle is responsible for keeping it in a roadworthy condition. This includes regular maintenance and fixing any known defects.

umwelt-14.question: How often should you, as the driver, roughly check the oil level and coolant?

options.a: Regularly, for example before longer trips or at fixed intervals
options.b: Only once when buying the car
options.c: Never, the engine handles it automatically
options.d: Only when a warning light comes on in the dashboard

umwelt-14.explanation: Anyone who regularly checks the oil level and coolant will spot problems early and avoid engine damage or breakdowns on longer trips.

umwelt-15.question: What indicates that the brake fluid should be replaced?

options.a: A squeaking noise when braking, which always indicates worn-out brake fluid
options.b: Brake fluid only needs to be changed based on mileage, regardless of its condition
options.c: The brake pedal feels soft or spongy
options.d: A darker colour of the brake fluid is purely cosmetic and has no meaning

umwelt-15.explanation: Brake fluid absorbs moisture over time, which can weaken braking performance. A soft or spongy brake pedal is a warning sign that should be checked at a workshop.

umwelt-16.question: What must you do if a headlight bulb on your car has failed?

options.a: Nothing, as long as the other side still lights up
options.b: Have it repaired as soon as possible, since full lighting matters for road safety
options.c: Only drive in daylight, then it doesn't matter
options.d: Wait until the second bulb fails too, then have both replaced at the same time

umwelt-16.explanation: Proper lighting is important so you can see and be seen by others. A faulty bulb should therefore be replaced promptly.

umwelt-17.question: What does the environmental zone (emissions sticker) regulate in many German city centres?

options.a: Only vehicles with a sufficient sticker (usually green) may enter the zone, to improve air quality
options.b: The sticker only applies to trucks; cars may always enter regardless of the sticker
options.c: Vehicles without a sticker may enter if they drive especially slowly
options.d: The sticker only needs to be shown at the annual technical inspection, not while driving

umwelt-17.explanation: Only vehicles with a sufficient emissions sticker may drive in environmental zones. This is meant to reduce air pollution from vehicle exhaust in heavily polluted city centres. Driving without the required sticker can lead to a fine, regardless of the speed driven.

umwelt-18.question: Why should you have the antifreeze in the coolant checked in winter?

options.a: So the engine warms up faster in winter
options.b: So the coolant doesn't freeze in frost and damage the engine
options.c: So the coolant evaporates faster in summer
options.d: It has no technical use, only a cosmetic one

umwelt-18.explanation: Without enough antifreeze, the coolant can freeze in hard frost and damage the engine. Checking it in good time before winter prevents costly damage.

umwelt-19.question: What effect does unnecessarily running the air conditioning have on fuel consumption?

options.a: It has no measurable effect
options.b: It lowers consumption because the engine stays cooler
options.c: It increases consumption because it needs extra engine power
options.d: It only affects consumption on trips shorter than 10 minutes

umwelt-19.explanation: The air conditioning is driven by the engine and needs extra energy for that. Using it only when needed saves fuel.

umwelt-20.question: Why can incorrectly set tyre pressure affect driving safety?

options.a: It changes the tyre's contact area with the road and therefore grip and braking
options.b: It only affects how the tyre looks
options.c: It only affects fuel consumption, not grip or braking distance
options.d: It changes nothing about grip or braking distance

umwelt-20.explanation: Tyre pressure that is too high or too low changes the tyre's contact patch on the road. This directly affects grip, handling, and braking distance.

umwelt-21.question: Which simple measure most reduces CO2 emissions over time, whether buying a car or driving one?

options.a: Regularly driving at high engine speed
options.b: Always using the window instead of ventilation, at any speed
options.c: Only avoiding unnecessary short cold starts, nothing else matters
options.d: Driving economically, maintaining the vehicle regularly, and avoiding unnecessary trips

umwelt-21.explanation: Economical driving, regular maintenance, and avoiding unnecessary trips clearly reduce fuel consumption and therefore CO2 emissions over time.

umwelt-22.question: What technical purpose does the headrest in a car serve?

options.a: It is only meant for comfort
options.b: It reduces the risk of whiplash injury in a rear-end collision
options.c: It replaces the seatbelt on short trips
options.d: It only protects in a head-on collision, not in a rear-end collision

umwelt-22.explanation: In a rear-end collision, the head is thrown backward and then forward very fast. A correctly adjusted headrest reduces the risk of whiplash injury.

umwelt-23.question: Why should tyres be checked regularly for uneven wear?

options.a: Uneven wear can point to incorrect wheel alignment or wrong tyre pressure
options.b: Uneven wear has no cause at all and is normal
options.c: Uneven wear only occurs on summer tyres, never on winter tyres
options.d: Uneven wear is only cosmetic; driving safety stays unaffected

umwelt-23.explanation: If a tyre is noticeably more worn on one side or spot, this often points to a technical issue like incorrect alignment or wrong pressure. It should be checked at a workshop.

umwelt-24.question: Why is unnecessary noise from a vehicle, such as heavily revving the engine, prohibited?

options.a: Because a loud engine noise automatically indicates a technical defect
options.b: Because it is only prohibited at night
options.c: Because avoidable noise needlessly disturbs other people
options.d: Because it is only a problem in traffic-calmed areas, and is allowed everywhere else

umwelt-24.explanation: Avoidable noise, such as heavy acceleration or unnecessarily revving the engine, disturbs residents and other road users and should be avoided.

umwelt-25.question: What environmental advantage does carpooling offer?

options.a: It has no effect since each car still drives individually
options.b: Fewer vehicles on the road mean lower total consumption and fewer emissions
options.c: The effect is only noticeable on very long trips over 500 kilometres
options.d: It is only worthwhile for electric cars

umwelt-25.explanation: When several people share one vehicle for the same route, fewer cars drive overall. This lowers total fuel consumption and emissions per person.

verhalten-01.question: A police officer at an intersection raises one arm straight up. What does this signal mean?

options.a: All vehicles from every direction must stop
options.b: Only vehicles coming from the right must stop
options.c: Traffic may continue as normal
options.d: The traffic light is about to turn green

verhalten-01.explanation: A vertically raised arm is the general attention signal: all traffic from every direction must stop.

verhalten-02.question: A police officer stretches one arm out to the side. Who must stop?

options.a: Only the traffic that crosses the path of the outstretched arm
options.b: Only oncoming traffic
options.c: All traffic from every direction
options.d: No one, the signal only applies to pedestrians

verhalten-02.explanation: An arm stretched out to the side acts like a red light for traffic crossing the arm's line. Traffic running parallel to the arm may continue.

verhalten-03.question: Traffic suddenly backs up ahead of you behind a hill crest. When should you switch on the hazard lights?

options.a: Briefly, to warn following vehicles of the sudden end of the traffic jam
options.b: Never, hazard lights are only allowed for breakdowns
options.c: Only if the police explicitly order it
options.d: Only after you have already crashed into the car ahead

verhalten-03.explanation: When a traffic jam suddenly ends or you brake hard, you may briefly switch on the hazard lights to warn following vehicles.

verhalten-04.question: You are towing a broken-down vehicle. What speed rule applies?

options.a: You may drive at most 40 km/h, unless a lower limit is posted
options.b: There is no speed limit at all when towing
options.c: You must drive at least 60 km/h to keep the tow rope taut
options.d: You may only exceed 30 km/h on the motorway

verhalten-04.explanation: When towing, a maximum speed of 40 km/h generally applies, unless a lower speed limit is in force.

verhalten-05.question: You sit behind the wheel of the towed vehicle while a tow rope is used. What applies?

options.a: You must be able to steer and brake, and you need a valid driving licence for this
options.b: You do not need a driving licence because the engine is off
options.c: You may take your hands off the wheel, the rope keeps you in lane
options.d: You must start the engine and accelerate along with the towing car

verhalten-05.explanation: Anyone steering a towed vehicle must hold a valid driving licence and be able to steer and brake the vehicle at all times.

verhalten-06.question: You are the first to arrive at a road accident with injured people. What must you do first?

options.a: Secure the accident scene, then give first aid and call the emergency services
options.b: Drive on immediately, since you did not cause the accident
options.c: Just take a photo and wait for others to react
options.d: Call your own insurance company before getting out of the car

verhalten-06.explanation: Anyone arriving at an accident must secure the scene, give first aid within their abilities, and alert the emergency services. Failing to help is a criminal offence.

verhalten-07.question: Roughly how far ahead of a broken-down vehicle on the motorway should you place the warning triangle?

options.a: About 100 metres in front of the vehicle
options.b: Directly next to the vehicle
options.c: About 5 metres in front of the vehicle
options.d: The warning triangle is not needed on the motorway

verhalten-07.explanation: On the motorway, the warning triangle should be placed much earlier due to high speeds, roughly 100 metres before the obstruction, so following vehicles have time to react.

verhalten-08.question: You are stopped at a red light with the engine running. May you briefly pick up your phone to read a message?

options.a: No, holding a mobile phone is forbidden while the engine runs, even standing still
options.b: Yes, as long as the light is red it is allowed
options.c: Yes, as long as the call lasts less than one minute
options.d: Yes, if no other vehicle is nearby

verhalten-08.explanation: A mobile phone may only be used while the engine is switched off. While the engine is running, the ban also applies when standing still at a red light.

verhalten-09.question: By law, who in the car must wear a seatbelt while driving?

options.a: Only the driver
options.b: Only the people in the front seats
options.c: Every occupant on every seat that has a seatbelt
options.d: Only children under twelve

verhalten-09.explanation: The seatbelt requirement applies to every occupant on every seat fitted with a belt, including passengers in the back seats.

verhalten-10.question: A six-year-old child under 150 cm tall is going to ride in the car. What applies?

options.a: A normal seatbelt is enough, a child seat is not required
options.b: The child needs a suitable child restraint system such as a child seat
options.c: The child may only ride on an adult's lap
options.d: Children under ten may generally not ride in a car at all

verhalten-10.explanation: Children under 12 and shorter than 150 cm must be secured in a suitable child restraint system.

verhalten-11.question: What must you make absolutely sure of before overtaking on a country road?

options.a: That the oncoming lane is visible far enough ahead and the manoeuvre fits safely
options.b: That your vehicle can drive faster than 100 km/h
options.c: That the driver ahead indicates and agrees
options.d: That there are fewer than three oncoming vehicles

verhalten-11.explanation: Before overtaking, the oncoming lane must be visible far enough ahead so the whole manoeuvre can be completed without endangering oncoming traffic.

verhalten-12.question: You are approaching a pedestrian crossing. May you overtake another vehicle right before it?

options.a: Yes, as long as no pedestrian is visible
options.b: No, overtaking is forbidden immediately before a pedestrian crossing
options.c: Yes, if you honk your horn first
options.d: Only outside built-up areas

verhalten-12.explanation: Overtaking is forbidden immediately before and at pedestrian crossings, because it could block the view of pedestrians.

verhalten-13.question: When are you allowed to use the horn in a built-up area?

options.a: Only to warn others of an immediate danger
options.b: Whenever you are annoyed with another road user
options.c: To tell a slow driver to speed up
options.d: To greet friends standing at the roadside

verhalten-13.explanation: The horn (audible warning) may only be used to warn others of an imminent danger, not to express annoyance.

verhalten-14.question: In which situation must you switch on dipped headlights during the day?

options.a: At dusk, in fog, in heavy rain, or in tunnels
options.b: Only at night after 10 p.m.
options.c: Only if the police order it
options.d: Never, daytime running lights are always enough

verhalten-14.explanation: Dipped headlights must be switched on at dusk, in fog, snowfall, heavy rain, or in tunnels, because daytime running lights are not enough and give no visibility from behind.

verhalten-15.question: You want to make a U-turn on a normal road. What must you observe?

options.a: You may only turn if you do not endanger or obstruct other traffic while doing so
options.b: U-turns are generally forbidden on all roads
options.c: A U-turn is only allowed with the hazard lights switched on
options.d: A U-turn is only allowed at junctions with traffic lights

verhalten-15.explanation: Anyone making a U-turn must be especially careful and must neither endanger nor unnecessarily obstruct other road users. On the motorway, U-turns are generally forbidden.

verhalten-16.question: You must reverse out of a narrow driveway onto the road and visibility is poor. What is correct?

options.a: Have someone guide you, or get out and check the area before reversing
options.b: Reverse quickly so the manoeuvre stays short
options.c: Looking in the rear-view mirror alone is always enough
options.d: Reversing on public roads is generally forbidden

verhalten-16.explanation: In poor visibility, you should have someone guide you or, if necessary, get out and check the area behind the vehicle before reversing.

verhalten-17.question: You are on a wide one-way street with no stopping or parking signs. Where may you park?

options.a: Only on the right-hand side in the direction of travel
options.b: On either the right or the left side, if the street is wide enough
options.c: Only with express permission from local residents
options.d: Parking is generally forbidden on one-way streets

verhalten-17.explanation: On one-way streets, unlike normal roads, parking is also allowed on the left side if the street is wide enough for it.

verhalten-18.question: You are driving in a roundabout and want to leave at the next exit. When must you indicate?

options.a: Only shortly before leaving the roundabout, to the right
options.b: Already when entering the roundabout, to the left
options.c: The whole time inside the roundabout, to the left
options.d: Indicating in a roundabout is generally not necessary

verhalten-18.explanation: Generally you do not indicate when entering a roundabout. Shortly before leaving it, you signal with the right indicator that you are exiting.

verhalten-19.question: You approach a railway crossing without barriers or flashing lights, but you see a train coming. What must you do?

options.a: Stop immediately, even though no warning signal is active
options.b: Speed up to cross the tracks before the train arrives
options.c: Keep going as long as the crossing lights are not flashing
options.d: Just honk and slowly roll forward

verhalten-19.explanation: A visibly approaching train requires you to stop, regardless of whether a technical warning system has already been triggered.

verhalten-20.question: On a two-lane motorway a traffic jam forms and an emergency vehicle needs to pass. How do you form an emergency corridor?

options.a: The left lane moves as far left as possible, all other lanes move as far right as possible
options.b: All vehicles move as far right as possible
options.c: All vehicles move as far left as possible
options.d: Only the right lane needs to move, the left lane stays where it is

verhalten-20.explanation: In slow-moving or stationary traffic on motorways and multi-lane roads, the leftmost lane must move left and all other lanes must move right, creating a corridor in the middle.

verhalten-21.question: You are driving in a long line of vehicles behind several trucks on a country road. How should you behave?

options.a: Keep right and let faster vehicles overtake as soon as it is safely possible
options.b: Drive side by side with the vehicle next to you to block overtaking
options.c: Keep honking so the trucks drive faster
options.d: Tailgate closely so no one can merge in between the vehicles

verhalten-21.explanation: The keep-right rule still applies within a convoy. Drivers who do not want to overtake themselves should let faster vehicles pass rather than blocking them.

verhalten-22.question: You are driving and want to briefly glance at your phone, which is mounted in a holder on the dashboard. Is that allowed?

options.a: Yes, as long as the phone stays in the holder and you do not pick it up
options.b: Yes, as long as you only look for 2 seconds
options.c: No, you may never look at a screen while driving, even in a holder
options.d: Only allowed if a passenger is in the car

verhalten-22.explanation: Glancing at a phone that is securely mounted is allowed as long as you do not pick it up or hold it; it must still be usable safely.

verhalten-23.question: A police officer directs traffic with hand signals at an intersection that also has traffic lights. What applies?

options.a: The officer's hand signals always take priority over the traffic light
options.b: The traffic light still applies; the officer is only assisting
options.c: You may choose for yourself which signal to follow
options.d: Both signals apply together; if they conflict you must stop and wait

verhalten-23.explanation: A police officer's hand signals always take priority over traffic lights and road signs.

verhalten-24.question: A school bus stops with its hazard lights on and children are getting off. How do you behave as a driver approaching or following?

options.a: Pass only at walking pace and be ready to stop if needed
options.b: Keep driving at normal speed as long as no child is on the road
options.c: Overtake as long as the oncoming lane is clear
options.d: Honk so the children hurry up

verhalten-24.explanation: When passing a stopped school bus with hazard lights on, you must drive at walking pace, because children may suddenly and carelessly step onto the road.

verhalten-25.question: What may the hard shoulder of a motorway be used for?

options.a: Only for emergencies, such as a breakdown or to make room for rescue services
options.b: As an extra driving lane during heavy traffic
options.c: For a short rest when feeling tired
options.d: For making a phone call without a hands-free system

verhalten-25.explanation: The hard shoulder is not a regular driving lane. It may only be used in emergencies, such as a breakdown or to make room for emergency vehicles.

zeichen-26.question: A round white sign with a red border shows a number followed by 't' (e.g. '7.5t', sign 262). What does it mean?

options.a: Vehicles heavier than the stated actual weight are banned from entering
options.b: A minimum weight is required to enter
options.c: A speed limit for heavy vehicles
options.d: A recommended load weight

zeichen-26.explanation: Sign 262 bans entry for vehicles whose actual weight exceeds the stated number, for example to protect a weak bridge.

zeichen-27.question: A round white sign with a red border shows two arrows marking a height in metres (sign 265). What does it mean?

options.a: Vehicles taller than the stated height are banned
options.b: Information about an especially tall bridge
options.c: A minimum height required for trucks
options.d: A recommended loading height

zeichen-27.explanation: Sign 265 bans entry for vehicles taller than the stated figure, for example before low bridges or underpasses.

zeichen-28.question: A round white sign with a red border shows a double-headed arrow with a width in metres (sign 264). What does it mean?

options.a: Vehicles wider than the stated width are banned
options.b: Information about an especially wide road
options.c: A minimum width required for trucks
options.d: A prescribed distance from the road edge

zeichen-28.explanation: Sign 264 bans entry for vehicles wider than the stated figure, for example before narrow tunnels.

zeichen-29.question: A round white sign with a red border shows a black truck next to a red car with '3.5t' added (sign 277). What does it mean?

options.a: A ban on overtaking for motor vehicles with a permitted total weight above 3.5 t
options.b: A ban on entering for trucks above 3.5 t
options.c: A parking ban for trucks above 3.5 t
options.d: A loading ban for vehicles above 3.5 t

zeichen-29.explanation: Sign 277 bans heavy motor vehicles over 3.5 t from overtaking other vehicles, often to avoid long, risky overtaking manoeuvres.

zeichen-30.question: A round white sign with a red border shows a black walking figure (sign 259). What does it mean?

options.a: Pedestrians are banned
options.b: A pedestrian zone begins
options.c: Pedestrians have priority
options.d: Caution, pedestrians may appear

zeichen-30.explanation: Sign 259 bans pedestrians from entering the road, for example on motorways or roads reserved for motor vehicles.

zeichen-31.question: A round white sign with a red border shows a black bicycle (sign 254). What does it mean?

options.a: Cyclists are banned
options.b: A bike path begins
options.c: A bicycle rental is nearby
options.d: Cyclists have priority

zeichen-31.explanation: Sign 254 bans cyclists from using the road, for example on motorways or roads reserved for motor vehicles.

zeichen-32.question: A blue rectangular sign with a white bicycle symbol and the word 'Fahrradstraße' (sign 244.1) means:

options.a: Cyclists may ride here, but cars have priority
options.b: The street is primarily meant for cyclists, motor vehicles may only use it if specifically allowed
options.c: Bicycles are banned on this street
options.d: It is a normal bike path next to the road

zeichen-32.explanation: A bicycle street is primarily meant for cyclists. Motor vehicles may only use it if an additional sign explicitly allows it, and must take special care.

zeichen-33.question: A blue round sign with three white arrows arranged in a circle (sign 215) means:

options.a: A roundabout, driving direction around the circle is mandatory
options.b: Entering a roundabout is banned
options.c: A motorway interchange lies ahead
options.d: A one-way street usable in both directions

zeichen-33.explanation: Sign 215 marks a roundabout and requires drivers to travel around it in the direction shown by the arrows.

zeichen-34.question: A blue rectangular sign with white symbols of a house, a shopping bag and a pedestrian (sign 242.1) indicates:

options.a: The start of a pedestrian zone
options.b: The end of a pedestrian zone
options.c: The start of a traffic-calmed area for cars
options.d: A shopping centre in 500 metres

zeichen-34.explanation: Sign 242.1 marks the start of a pedestrian zone, where motor vehicles are generally not allowed to drive.

zeichen-35.question: The same sign as the start of a pedestrian zone, but crossed out in grey (sign 242.2), means:

options.a: The end of the pedestrian zone
options.b: The start of a second pedestrian area
options.c: The pedestrian zone is only valid at night from here
options.d: A warning of many pedestrians

zeichen-35.explanation: The crossed-out sign 242.2 marks the end of the pedestrian zone. From here on, normal traffic rules apply again.

zeichen-36.question: A triangular warning sign showing a car skidding sideways (sign 114) warns of:

options.a: A risk of skidding, for example due to loose grit or ice
options.b: A sharp bend ahead
options.c: An upcoming tyre change point
options.d: Strong crosswinds

zeichen-36.explanation: Sign 114 warns of a skidding or slipping hazard, for example due to loose chippings, oil, or ice, and calls for careful, anticipatory driving.

zeichen-37.question: A triangular warning sign showing rocks and falling stones warns of:

options.a: Possible falling rocks or stones on the road
options.b: A cave nearby
options.c: Roadworks involving blasting
options.d: A nature reserve

zeichen-37.explanation: The warning sign with a falling-rocks symbol marks a stretch of road where stones or rocks can fall onto the carriageway, for example along steep rock faces.

zeichen-38.question: A triangular warning sign showing a windsock blown to the side (sign 117) warns of:

options.a: Strong crosswinds that can push the vehicle sideways
options.b: A cyclist filtering lane
options.c: Storm damage at the roadside
options.d: A ferry crossing the river

zeichen-38.explanation: Sign 117 warns of strong crosswinds, which can push tall vehicles such as motorhomes or trucks out of their lane.

zeichen-39.question: A triangular warning sign with a wavy line on the road surface (sign 112) means:

options.a: An uneven road surface, for example bumps or potholes
options.b: A wave-shaped bridge
options.c: A river crosses the road
options.d: A winding stretch of road ahead

zeichen-39.explanation: Sign 112 warns of an uneven road surface with bumps or potholes, which can make the vehicle handle unpredictably.

zeichen-40.question: A triangular warning sign showing a leaping animal (sign 142) warns of:

options.a: Wild animals that may suddenly cross the road
options.b: A zoo nearby
options.c: An unfenced pasture next to the road
options.d: An animal shelter nearby

zeichen-40.explanation: Sign 142 warns of wild animals crossing. Especially at dusk and in wooded areas, animals can suddenly run onto the road.

zeichen-41.question: A triangular warning sign with a black saltire on a yellow background (sign 102) warns of:

options.a: A crossroads or junction where priority-to-the-right applies
options.b: A railway crossing with barriers
options.c: A priority road that continues
options.d: The end of a priority road with no further meaning

zeichen-41.explanation: This sign warns of an upcoming crossroads or junction with no priority signs, so the priority-to-the-right rule applies.

zeichen-42.question: Before a motorway exit there is a large rectangular sign showing several lanes and destinations, well ahead of the actual exit. What is this sign called?

options.a: An advance direction sign, showing early which lane leads to which destination
options.b: A town-entry sign
options.c: A traffic-calmed area
options.d: An additional sign for a speed limit

zeichen-42.explanation: The advance direction sign tells drivers early on which lane leads to which destination, so they can position themselves in good time.

zeichen-43.question: You pass a yellow rectangular sign with a town name in black lettering (sign 310, town-entry sign). What applies from here, unless another sign says otherwise?

options.a: The general speed limit inside built-up areas of 50 km/h applies
options.b: Unlimited speed applies from here
options.c: A 30 km/h limit automatically applies from here
options.d: The town-entry sign has no effect on speed

zeichen-43.explanation: The town-entry sign marks the start of a built-up area. Without an additional sign, the general in-town speed limit of 50 km/h applies from here.

zeichen-44.question: The same yellow sign with the town name, but crossed out in grey (sign 311), means:

options.a: The end of the built-up area, the in-town speed limit ends here
options.b: The start of a second part of the town
options.c: The town name no longer applies for navigation systems from here
options.d: The start of a traffic-calmed area

zeichen-44.explanation: The crossed-out town sign marks the end of the built-up area. From here, the higher out-of-town speed limit applies again, unless another sign states otherwise.

zeichen-45.question: Under a parking sign (sign 314) there is an additional sign showing a parking disc and '2 Std'. What must you do?

options.a: Set your arrival time on a parking disc and stay for a maximum of two hours
options.b: Nothing, the sign is just a recommendation
options.c: Buy a ticket from a machine within two hours
options.d: Only park between 2 and 3 a.m.

zeichen-45.explanation: The additional sign with a parking disc and time limit means you must set your arrival time on a parking disc and must not exceed the maximum parking duration.

zeichen-46.question: Legally, what is the difference between 'stopping' and 'parking' under German traffic law?

options.a: Stopping is standing still for up to three minutes, parking is any longer stay or leaving the vehicle
options.b: There is legally no difference between stopping and parking
options.c: Stopping is only allowed with hazard lights on, parking never is
options.d: Parking is only allowed at night, stopping only during the day

zeichen-46.explanation: Stopping means standing still for at most three minutes without leaving the vehicle. If it lasts longer, or the driver leaves the vehicle, it counts as parking. A no-stopping sign forbids both, a no-parking sign still allows brief stopping.

zeichen-47.question: A blue rectangular sign on the motorway with a large 'exit' arrow and a number (sign 333) indicates:

options.a: The next motorway exit, at the stated distance
options.b: The start of a rest area
options.c: The end of the motorway
options.d: Roadworks coming up shortly

zeichen-47.explanation: Sign 333 announces an upcoming motorway exit and usually shows the distance to it in metres.

zeichen-48.question: A rectangular blue sign with a white border showing a house, playing children and a vehicle (sign 325.1) announces:

options.a: The start of a traffic-calmed zone, where pedestrians have priority and walking pace applies
options.b: The start of a pedestrian zone with no motor vehicles
options.c: A residential area with a 30 km/h limit
options.d: A playground with no traffic

zeichen-48.explanation: In a traffic-calmed zone, pedestrians may use the whole area and have priority. Vehicles may only travel at walking pace.

zeichen-49.question: A round white sign with a red border shows '30' under the heading 'Tempo 30 Zone' (sign 274.1). How long does this speed limit apply?

options.a: For the entire zone, until a sign marked 'End of 30 km/h zone' appears
options.b: Only exactly where the sign is placed
options.c: Only until the next junction
options.d: Only between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.

zeichen-49.explanation: Unlike a single speed-limit sign, a zone sign applies to the whole area until the matching end-of-zone sign, even across several junctions.

zeichen-50.question: Under a 'no entry' sign there is an additional sign reading 'Anlieger frei' (residents/deliveries only). Who may still enter?

options.a: Only vehicles whose destination is a property or address within the restricted street
options.b: Anyone who wants to use the street as a shortcut
options.c: Only delivery trucks from logistics companies
options.d: No one, the additional sign has no practical meaning

zeichen-50.explanation: The 'Anlieger frei' additional sign only allows entry for destination traffic, meaning vehicles that actually have business there, not through-traffic using it as a shortcut.

autobahn-01.question: Can you take the motorway with a vehicle that cannot go faster than 55 km/h?

options.a: Yes, if you use the right-hand lane
options.b: No, such vehicles are not allowed on the motorway
options.c: Yes, but only at night when traffic is light
options.d: Yes, if you switch on the hazard lights

autobahn-01.explanation: Vehicles on the motorway must be able to reach a certain minimum speed. Vehicles that cannot are not allowed on it at all.

autobahn-02.question: Which of these vehicles is not allowed on the motorway?

options.a: A motorhome
options.b: A minibus
options.c: A moped
options.d: An estate car with a trailer

autobahn-02.explanation: Mopeds, bicycles and pedestrians are generally not allowed on the motorway, because they cannot reach the required minimum speed.

autobahn-03.question: You have missed your exit on the motorway. What must you do?

options.a: Keep driving to the next exit
options.b: Carefully reverse along the hard shoulder
options.c: Turn around on the carriageway if no traffic is coming
options.d: Reverse along the hard shoulder to reach the exit

autobahn-03.explanation: Turning around and reversing are forbidden on the motorway. A missed exit can only be corrected at the next exit.

autobahn-04.question: There is no general speed limit on the Autobahn. Are you still allowed to drive very slowly, for example 40 km/h?

options.a: Yes, driving slowly is always allowed on the Autobahn
options.b: No, unusually slow driving without a good reason is prohibited and endangers traffic
options.c: Yes, as long as you use the right-hand lane
options.d: No, a fixed minimum speed of 80 km/h applies to all vehicles

autobahn-04.explanation: Without a good reason (e.g. a breakdown, dense fog), you must not obstruct the flow of traffic by driving unnecessarily slowly.

autobahn-05.question: Traffic on the motorway suddenly slows right down. When must you form an emergency lane?

options.a: As soon as traffic slows to walking pace or comes to a stop
options.b: Only once an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is visible
options.c: Only once traffic has been stationary for more than ten minutes
options.d: Only when instructed by the police

autobahn-05.explanation: An emergency lane must be formed immediately once traffic slows to walking pace or stops, not only once an emergency vehicle appears.

autobahn-06.question: You want to leave the Autobahn via an exit. When should you move onto the deceleration lane?

options.a: Only just before the deceleration lane ends, to save time
options.b: In good time, as soon as the deceleration lane begins, not just at the end
options.c: Only if no other vehicle is behind you
options.d: You must slow to 30 km/h before changing lanes

autobahn-06.explanation: You should move onto the deceleration lane early and brake there, rather than braking on the through lane.

autobahn-07.question: On which side may you normally overtake on the motorway?

options.a: On whichever side has less traffic
options.b: Only on the left side
options.c: On either side, depending on which lane is free
options.d: Only on the right side

autobahn-07.explanation: Overtaking is generally only allowed on the left. Overtaking on the right is only permitted on the motorway when traffic on all lanes is jammed and moving slowly.

autobahn-08.question: You have just overtaken a vehicle. When may you move back to the right?

options.a: Only once you can see the overtaken vehicle clearly enough in your mirror
options.b: Immediately after passing it, so the left lane stays free
options.c: Only after you have switched off the indicator
options.d: Only once the overtaken vehicle honks

autobahn-08.explanation: You may only pull back in once the overtaken vehicle is clearly visible in your mirror, so you don't endanger it.

autobahn-09.question: The carriageway is divided into two lanes by a solid line. What does this mean for overtaking?

options.a: Overtaking is still allowed without restriction
options.b: Overtaking is only allowed with hazard lights on
options.c: The solid line must not be crossed to overtake
options.d: Overtaking is only allowed in daylight

autobahn-09.explanation: A solid line must not be crossed. While it applies, an overtaking manoeuvre that crosses it is forbidden.

autobahn-10.question: You are approaching a crest with poor visibility on a country road. May you overtake?

options.a: Yes, if no vehicle is behind you
options.b: No, because you cannot see oncoming traffic in time
options.c: Yes, if you are driving faster than 80 km/h
options.d: Yes, if you briefly honk your horn

autobahn-10.explanation: Overtaking is forbidden before crests and bends with poor visibility, because oncoming traffic would be spotted too late. This is one of the most dangerous causes of head-on collisions.

autobahn-11.question: It is raining heavily. You are overtaking a truck on the Autobahn. What must you especially watch out for?

options.a: Sudden loss of visibility from spray thrown up by the truck
options.b: Trucks do not produce extra spray in the rain
options.c: You only need to increase your speed to get past faster
options.d: The truck driver alone is responsible for ensuring enough visibility

autobahn-11.explanation: Trucks throw up a lot of water spray on wet roads, which can briefly and severely reduce visibility while overtaking.

autobahn-12.question: You overtake a cyclist outside built-up areas. What minimum lateral distance should you keep?

options.a: About 0.5 metres is enough
options.b: At least about 2 metres
options.c: One metre is enough if you drive slowly
options.d: Distance does not matter as long as you honk

autobahn-12.explanation: When overtaking cyclists, a lateral distance of at least about 1.5 metres inside and about 2 metres outside built-up areas must be kept.

autobahn-13.question: Why do you need more time and space to overtake a truck than a car?

options.a: Because the truck is much longer, which makes the overtaking distance longer
options.b: Because trucks always drive faster than cars
options.c: Because trucks do not have brake lights
options.d: Because trucks always have to drive in the left lane

autobahn-13.explanation: A truck is much longer than a car. That is why overtaking it takes longer and requires more clear road and a better view of oncoming traffic.

autobahn-14.question: A long convoy of several trucks is driving ahead of you. What must you especially watch out for when overtaking?
