options.a: The convoy may only be overtaken at a red traffic light
options.b: The overtaking manoeuvre takes much longer, so the road ahead must be clear and visible for a long enough distance
options.c: It is enough to overtake only the first truck and then pull back in
options.d: Convoys of trucks may generally never be overtaken

autobahn-14.explanation: Overtaking several vehicles in a row takes much longer. The road must stay clear and visible long enough to safely judge oncoming traffic.

autobahn-15.question: You are driving along the acceleration lane onto the motorway. What is the correct behaviour?

options.a: You merge onto the motorway and the other traffic must make room for you
options.b: You accelerate to match the speed of the flowing traffic and merge in when it is safe
options.c: You first drive slowly and stop at the end of the lane
options.d: You drive onto the left lane with your hazard lights switched on

autobahn-15.explanation: A driver joining via the acceleration lane must match the speed of motorway traffic and merge in as soon as a safe gap appears. Flowing traffic has priority.

autobahn-16.question: Where must you reduce your speed before leaving the motorway?

options.a: Only on the deceleration lane, not already on the through lane
options.b: Already on the right-hand through lane
options.c: Only after the end of the motorway, on the country road
options.d: Already 5 kilometres before the exit

autobahn-16.explanation: Speed may only be reduced on the deceleration lane, not on the through lane. Otherwise following traffic is caught off guard.

autobahn-17.question: Your vehicle breaks down on the motorway. What is correct?

options.a: You stay seated in the vehicle and wait for the police
options.b: You switch on the hazard lights, set up a warning triangle, put on a hi-vis vest, and wait behind the crash barrier
options.c: You push the vehicle onto the left lane yourself
options.d: You set up the warning triangle directly behind the vehicle, without a hi-vis vest

autobahn-17.explanation: In case of a breakdown on the motorway, hazard lights and a warning triangle set up far enough back secure the scene. You and your passengers should then take shelter behind the crash barrier.

autobahn-18.question: You are planning a motorway trip. Why should you fill up with enough fuel beforehand?

options.a: Because fuel stations are generally not allowed on motorways
options.b: Because stopping due to an empty tank on the motorway is an offence and can be very dangerous
options.c: Because the motorway is always longer than 500 km
options.d: Because refuelling is only allowed every 200 km

autobahn-18.explanation: Driving onto the motorway without enough fuel and breaking down is an offence. Stopping on the carriageway is also very dangerous for everyone involved.

autobahn-19.question: What does the recommended speed (Richtgeschwindigkeit) of 130 km/h on the motorway mean?

options.a: It is a fixed speed limit, and exceeding it triggers a fine
options.b: It only applies to trucks
options.c: It is a recommendation, not a binding maximum speed, but driving faster can increase liability in a crash
options.d: It only applies at night

autobahn-19.explanation: 130 km/h is not a fixed maximum speed but a recommendation. In a crash, driving faster can still increase a driver's share of the blame.

autobahn-20.question: What does the traffic sign 'no overtaking for motor vehicles of any kind' mean?

options.a: Only trucks are not allowed to overtake
options.b: No motor vehicle may overtake another vehicle until the prohibition ends
options.c: Overtaking is only forbidden in daylight
options.d: Overtaking is only forbidden for learner drivers

autobahn-20.explanation: The sign forbids all motor vehicles from overtaking until a sign lifts the prohibition again.

autobahn-21.question: You are driving through a tunnel on the motorway. What is correct?

options.a: The dipped headlights must be switched on
options.b: The safety distance may be shorter than usual
options.c: Listening to the radio is generally forbidden in tunnels
options.d: You may stop in the tunnel without reason to get your bearings

autobahn-21.explanation: Dipped headlights must be switched on in tunnels. It is also advisable to switch to a tunnel radio frequency to hear warnings, and to keep enough distance.

autobahn-22.question: You must suddenly brake hard on the motorway because of a traffic jam ahead. What should you also do?

options.a: Nothing, braking hard alone is enough
options.b: Flash your headlights repeatedly
options.c: Briefly switch on the hazard lights to warn following traffic
options.d: Swerve onto the hard shoulder to get more braking distance

autobahn-22.explanation: Briefly switching on the hazard lights alerts following vehicles to sudden hard braking and can help prevent rear-end collisions.

autobahn-23.question: You drive on the motorway permanently in the left lane without overtaking. Is that allowed?

options.a: Yes, as long as you drive no slower than 100 km/h
options.b: No, the left lane may only be used for overtaking
options.c: Yes, if there is a truck in the right lane
options.d: Yes, as long as you have your indicator on

autobahn-23.explanation: The keep-right rule applies. The left lane may only be used for overtaking, not for permanent driving.

autobahn-24.question: An object falls off your trailer onto the carriageway on the motorway. What must you do?

options.a: Stop in a safe place, warn other traffic, and have the object removed without putting yourself at risk
options.b: Stop immediately in the affected lane and pick up the object
options.c: Keep driving, because the load is not your responsibility
options.d: Only call the police and keep driving yourself

autobahn-24.explanation: The driver is responsible for the load. If something falls off, you must act safely without endangering yourself in flowing traffic.

autobahn-25.question: At a motorway roadworks site, one lane suddenly ends. How should vehicles on both lanes behave correctly?

options.a: All vehicles in the ending lane must merge immediately and far ahead of the narrowing
options.b: Vehicles merge alternately, using the zip merge, only shortly before the narrowing
options.c: The through lane must stop until everyone else has merged
options.d: Only trucks are allowed to change lanes

autobahn-25.explanation: In a zip merge, vehicles in both lanes drive up to shortly before the narrowing and then merge in alternately.

parken-01.question: What is the difference between 'stopping' (Halten) and 'parking' (Parken)?

options.a: Stopping is generally forbidden, parking is always allowed
options.b: You may only park with the hazard lights switched on
options.c: It counts as parking if you stand still for more than three minutes or leave the vehicle
options.d: Stopping is only allowed at night

parken-01.explanation: Standing still for more than three minutes or leaving the vehicle counts legally as parking. Briefer stops, for example to let someone in or out, count as stopping.

parken-02.question: How close to an intersection are you normally not allowed to park?

options.a: Within 1 metre before and after the intersection
options.b: Within 5 metres before and after the intersection
options.c: Within 20 metres before and after the intersection
options.d: Parking before intersections is allowed everywhere

parken-02.explanation: You may not park within 5 metres before and after an intersection or junction, so that visibility stays clear.

parken-03.question: May you park directly in front of a driveway?

options.a: No, that would block entering and exiting
options.b: Yes, as long as you stay less than ten minutes
options.c: Yes, as long as no sign explicitly forbids parking
options.d: Yes, as long as the owner cannot see it

parken-03.explanation: Parking in front of driveways is forbidden, because it would block access.

parken-04.question: You want to park on a narrow street. What must you pay attention to?

options.a: Only that your vehicle is not standing on the pavement
options.b: That enough space remains for other vehicles, including larger ones like ambulances, to pass through
options.c: That you allow at least two hours for the parking manoeuvre
options.d: That you park in the middle of the street so both sides have equal space

parken-04.explanation: On narrow streets, enough space must remain so that even larger vehicles like ambulances can still pass through.

parken-05.question: How close before a pedestrian crossing are you not allowed to park?

options.a: Within 1 metre before it
options.b: Within 5 metres before it
options.c: Within 20 metres before it
options.d: Parking before it is generally allowed

parken-05.explanation: You may not park within 5 metres before a pedestrian crossing, so that pedestrians and drivers can see each other in time.

parken-06.question: Who may use a specially marked disabled parking space?

options.a: Anyone who only stops briefly
options.b: Only vehicles with a valid disability parking permit or corresponding authorisation
options.c: Anyone with a large vehicle
options.d: Only vehicles with a trailer

parken-06.explanation: Disabled parking spaces are reserved only for vehicles with a valid permit or corresponding authorisation.

parken-07.question: May you park at night without lights?

options.a: No, never, regardless of the type of road
options.b: Yes, on sufficiently lit roads with a speed limit of up to 50 km/h
options.c: Yes, but only if the vehicle is painted red
options.d: Yes, as long as the driver's door is not locked

parken-07.explanation: On sufficiently lit roads with a speed limit of up to 50 km/h, parking is generally allowed without additional lights.

parken-08.question: What does 'double parking' mean?

options.a: Stopping alongside already parked vehicles so they get boxed in
options.b: Parking in two adjacent parking spaces at the same time
options.c: Parking with the rear of the vehicle facing the road
options.d: Parking that is only allowed on weekends

parken-08.explanation: Double parking blocks already parked vehicles and is forbidden, because it obstructs traffic and the boxed-in vehicles.

parken-09.question: On which type of street may you park on the left side in the direction of travel?

options.a: On any street
options.b: Only in a one-way street
options.c: Only on country roads
options.d: Only if another vehicle is already parked on the left

parken-09.explanation: Parking on the left is generally only allowed in one-way streets. On normal streets, you must park on the right side.

parken-10.question: You park in a zone requiring a parking disc. What must you do?

options.a: Set the actual arrival time and place the disc clearly visible behind the windscreen
options.b: Set any time that allows for longer parking
options.c: Only get the parking disc from the glovebox when checked
options.d: Only use a parking disc on weekdays

parken-10.explanation: The parking disc must show the actual arrival time and be clearly visible behind the windscreen, so the permitted parking duration can be checked.

parken-11.question: You are standing with your vehicle in a loading zone. When are you allowed to stay there?

options.a: For as long as you like, as long as you sit in the vehicle
options.b: Only at night
options.c: Only for as long as you are actually loading or unloading
options.d: Only if you have a trailer

parken-11.explanation: A loading zone may only be used for actual loading and unloading, not for ordinary parking.

parken-12.question: May you park your car on the pavement?

options.a: Yes, that is allowed everywhere if the pavement is wide enough
options.b: Only where a sign explicitly allows parking on the pavement
options.c: Yes, but only with two wheels on the pavement
options.d: Yes, if no pedestrians are around

parken-12.explanation: Parking on the pavement is only allowed where a sign explicitly permits it, for example the pavement-parking sign.

parken-13.question: Why are you not allowed to park directly in front of a fire hydrant?

options.a: Because the fire brigade needs immediate access to the hydrant in an emergency
options.b: Because the water could otherwise accidentally damage the car
options.c: Because hydrants are always located on private property
options.d: Because only bicycles may be left there

parken-13.explanation: The area in front of a hydrant must stay clear, so the fire brigade can connect a hose immediately in an emergency.

parken-14.question: In a short-term parking zone, the maximum duration is limited to one hour. What applies if you stay longer?

options.a: That is allowed, as long as the parking disc is visible
options.b: That is allowed, as long as a parking ticket was bought
options.c: That exceeds the permitted parking time and is a violation
options.d: That is allowed if nobody checks

parken-14.explanation: Exceeding the maximum duration stated on the sign is a parking violation, regardless of whether a parking disc is displayed.

parken-15.question: You stop briefly on a street where stopping is actually forbidden, and switch on the hazard lights. Is that allowed?

options.a: Yes, the hazard lights automatically make any stop legal
options.b: No, the hazard lights do not lift a no-stopping restriction
options.c: Yes, as long as you stay under one minute
options.d: Yes, as long as no other vehicles are nearby

parken-15.explanation: Switching on the hazard lights does not permit stopping where it is forbidden. It only warns other road users but does not lift a prohibition.

parken-16.question: You want to get out of your parked car. What must you do beforehand?

options.a: Only switch off the engine
options.b: Look back over your shoulder and make sure no cyclist or vehicle is approaching
options.c: Only check the rear-view mirror, one glance is always enough
options.d: Open the door immediately, because parked cars pose no danger to others

parken-16.explanation: Before getting out, you must make sure no cyclist or vehicle is passing. A carelessly opened door can seriously injure cyclists.

parken-17.question: You park facing uphill at a kerb with no barrier. How do you correctly turn the wheels?

options.a: Turn the front wheels towards the kerb
options.b: Turn the front wheels away from the road, towards the middle of the road
options.c: Always leave the wheels pointing straight ahead
options.d: Only turn the rear wheels

parken-17.explanation: When parking uphill, the front wheels are turned towards the kerb. If the vehicle rolls back unintentionally, it stops at the kerb.

parken-18.question: You park facing downhill at a kerb. How do you correctly turn the wheels?

options.a: Turn the front wheels away from the road, towards the middle of the road
options.b: Turn the front wheels towards the kerb
options.c: Always leave the wheels pointing straight ahead
options.d: Only use the handbrake, the wheels do not matter

parken-18.explanation: When parking downhill, the front wheels are turned towards the kerb. If the vehicle rolls forward unintentionally, it steers towards the kerb instead of into the road.

parken-19.question: May you park near a level crossing?

options.a: No, parking is forbidden in the area before and after a level crossing
options.b: Yes, as long as no train is in sight
options.c: Yes, if you switch on the hazard lights
options.d: Yes, as long as you stay in the vehicle

parken-19.explanation: Parking before and after level crossings is forbidden, because visibility and free access for vehicles and barriers must be kept clear at all costs.

parken-20.question: How close to a bus stop are you normally not allowed to park?

options.a: Within 5 metres
options.b: Within 15 metres before and after the bus stop sign
options.c: Within 1 metre
options.d: Parking at bus stops is generally allowed

parken-20.explanation: Parking is forbidden within 15 metres before and after a bus or tram stop sign.

parken-21.question: You are in a traffic-calmed zone (a 'play street'). Where may you park?

options.a: Anywhere, as long as the engine is running
options.b: Only directly in front of a playground
options.c: Only in the areas specifically marked for parking
options.d: Nowhere, parking is always forbidden there

parken-21.explanation: In a traffic-calmed zone, you may only park in the areas specifically marked for it, so that playing children and pedestrians keep enough space.

parken-22.question: May you park in front of a fire station entrance or an area marked as a fire lane?

options.a: Yes, as long as it is night-time
options.b: No, these access routes must remain clear at all times
options.c: Yes, as long as no emergency vehicle is visible
options.d: Yes, for a maximum of five minutes

parken-22.explanation: Fire lanes and access routes to fire stations must remain clear at all times, so emergency vehicles can leave without delay.

parken-23.question: You park outside built-up areas on an unlit road. What must you take into account?

options.a: The vehicle needs parking lights or must be recognisable by reflectors
options.b: Lighting is never needed there, because there is barely any traffic
options.c: It is enough to cover the vehicle with a blanket
options.d: Lighting is only needed when it rains

parken-23.explanation: Outside built-up areas on unlit roads, a parked vehicle must be clearly recognisable to others through lighting or reflectors.

parken-24.question: You want to stop briefly to let a passenger out, in an area with restricted no-stopping rules. Is that allowed?

options.a: No, a restricted no-stopping zone forbids any stop without exception
options.b: Yes, briefly stopping to let someone in or out is allowed even under restricted no-stopping rules
options.c: Yes, but only with prior police approval
options.d: No, that is only allowed on motorways

parken-24.explanation: A restricted no-stopping zone still allows briefly stopping to let someone in or out, as long as the driver stays ready to move on. A full no-stopping zone, however, forbids any stop.

parken-25.question: May you leave your car on a bike lane?

options.a: Yes, as long as you only go shopping briefly
options.b: Yes, as long as the hazard lights are switched on
options.c: No, bike lanes must remain clear for cyclists
options.d: Yes, if no other parking space is free

parken-25.explanation: Bike lanes are for cyclists and must remain clear. Parking on a bike lane forces cyclists to dangerously swerve into flowing car traffic.

zeichen-51.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.a: The road bends to the right.
options.b: The road first bends left, then right.
options.c: The road narrows on one side.
options.d: You must give way to oncoming traffic.

zeichen-51.explanation: Sign 103 warns of a curve that bends to the right. Adjust your speed in good time.

zeichen-52.question: What does this traffic sign show?

options.a: A single right-hand curve.
options.b: A double curve, first to the left.
options.c: A road narrowing.
options.d: A steep downgrade.

zeichen-52.explanation: Sign 105 warns of a double curve. The road first bends left, then right.

zeichen-53.question: What does this sign with the percentage mean?

options.a: The road rises steeply.
options.b: The road descends steeply.
options.c: The road surface is uneven.
options.d: There is a risk of skidding when wet.

zeichen-54.question: What does this sign mean?

options.a: The road descends steeply.
options.b: The road rises steeply.
options.c: A sharp curve follows.
options.d: A traffic jam follows.

zeichen-54.explanation: Sign 110 warns of a steep upgrade. The percentage shows the gradient, here for example 10%.

zeichen-55.question: What does this sign warn of?

options.a: An uneven road surface.
options.b: A risk of skidding when wet.
options.c: A road narrowing.
options.d: Falling rocks.

zeichen-55.explanation: Sign 112 warns of an uneven road surface, for example bumps or potholes.

zeichen-56.question: What does this sign warn of?

options.a: Wild animals crossing.
options.b: A risk of skidding or slipping, for example due to wetness or leaves.
options.c: A sharp curve.
options.d: A railway crossing.

zeichen-56.explanation: Sign 114 warns of a risk of skidding or slipping. Adjust your speed and driving style to the road surface.

zeichen-57.question: What does this sign warn of?

options.a: Crosswind.
options.b: Falling rocks.
options.c: Oncoming traffic.
options.d: A steep upgrade.

zeichen-57.explanation: Sign 117 warns of strong crosswind, which can be especially dangerous for tall vehicles and motorcycles.

zeichen-58.question: What does this sign mean?

options.a: The road narrows on both sides.
options.b: The road narrows on one side, from the right.
options.c: Roadworks follow.
options.d: Oncoming traffic on a narrow road.

zeichen-58.explanation: Sign 121 warns of a road that narrows on only one side. Expect traffic to merge.

zeichen-59.question: What does this sign warn of?

options.a: A traffic queue ahead.
options.b: A traffic light ahead.
options.c: Oncoming traffic.
options.d: A road narrowing.

zeichen-59.explanation: Sign 124 warns of a traffic queue. Reduce speed early and watch the traffic ahead of you.

zeichen-60.question: What does this sign warn of?

options.a: Oncoming traffic, for example at a narrow section.
options.b: A traffic queue.
options.c: An intersection with priority from the right.
options.d: A railway crossing.

zeichen-60.explanation: Sign 125 warns of oncoming traffic, for example where a previously separated carriageway becomes two-way again.

zeichen-61.question: What does this sign warn of?

options.a: A traffic light ahead.
options.b: A railway crossing.
options.c: A pedestrian crossing.
options.d: A roundabout.

zeichen-61.explanation: Sign 131 warns of a traffic light that is hard to see from a distance.

zeichen-62.question: What does this sign warn of?

options.a: Cyclists crossing or joining the road.
options.b: A pedestrian crossing.
options.c: Children.
options.d: A cycle street.

zeichen-62.explanation: Sign 138 warns of places where cyclists often cross or join the road.

zeichen-63.question: What does this sign warn of?

options.a: Wild animals crossing.
options.b: A curve.
options.c: Falling rocks.
options.d: A bridle path.

zeichen-63.explanation: Sign 142 warns of wild animals crossing. Especially at dusk, expect animals to run onto the road suddenly.

zeichen-64.question: What does this sign warn of?

options.a: A pedestrian crossing ahead.
options.b: Children playing.
options.c: A pedestrian zone.
options.d: A roundabout with many pedestrians.

zeichen-64.explanation: Sign 101-21 gives advance warning of a pedestrian crossing. It is a warning sign, placed before the actual Zeichen 293, which marks the crossing itself.

zeichen-65.question: What does this sign warn of?

options.a: Falling rocks.
options.b: An uneven road surface.
options.c: Wild animals crossing.
options.d: A closed mountain road.

zeichen-65.explanation: Sign 101-25 warns of falling rocks, for example on roads below rocky slopes.

zeichen-66.question: What does this sign with three red stripes mean?

options.a: A railway crossing follows in about 240 metres.
options.b: You have already reached the railway crossing.
options.c: The railway crossing is closed.
options.d: A railway crossing follows in about 80 metres.

zeichen-66.explanation: Sign 156 is a three-stripe marker post before a railway crossing without barriers. The number of stripes decreases with distance: three stripes at about 240 m, two at 160 m, one at 80 m.

zeichen-67.question: What does this traffic sign mean at a junction?

options.a: You may not turn at this junction.
options.b: At this junction you must continue in the direction shown.
options.c: The junction is closed to vehicles.
options.d: It is only a recommendation you do not have to follow.

zeichen-67.explanation: Sign 211 mandates a specific direction of travel at this junction.

zeichen-68.question: What does this traffic sign prescribe?

options.a: You must continue here either straight ahead or turn right.
options.b: You may only turn right here.
options.c: Driving straight ahead is prohibited here.
options.d: You may drive in any direction here.

zeichen-68.explanation: Zeichen 214 is a mandatory sign for prescribed direction of travel: at this point you may only continue straight ahead or turn right - all other directions (e.g. turning left or making a U-turn) are prohibited.

zeichen-69.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.a: The obstacle may only be passed on the side shown.
options.b: The obstacle may be passed on either side.
options.c: It is an overtaking ban for the whole stretch of road.

zeichen-70.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.a: Riders on horseback prohibited.

zeichen-71.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

zeichen-72.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.d: Caution, icy/snowy road.

zeichen-73.question: What does this traffic sign with the number 30 mean?

zeichen-74.question: What does this traffic sign mean (white and red arrow pointing in opposite directions)?

options.b: Oncoming traffic is prohibited.
options.c: You have priority over oncoming traffic, which must wait.
options.d: It marks a one-way street.

zeichen-74.explanation: Sign 308 shows that your direction of travel (white arrow) has priority over oncoming traffic (red arrow), for example at a narrowed section of road.

zeichen-75.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.a: No motor vehicles.
options.b: No bicycles.
options.c: No pedestrians.
options.d: No motorcycles.

zeichen-75.explanation: Sign 251 prohibits entry for cars and other multi-track motor vehicles.

zeichen-76.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

zeichen-77.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

zeichen-81.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

zeichen-82.explanation: Sign 259 prohibits pedestrians from entering the road.

zeichen-83.question: What does this traffic sign with a weight value mean?

options.a: Maximum axle load as shown.

zeichen-84.question: What does this traffic sign with a width value mean?

zeichen-85.question: What does this traffic sign with a height value mean?

options.a: No vehicles taller than the value shown.

options.d: Bridge height as shown.

zeichen-85.explanation: Sign 265 prohibits entry for vehicles taller than the value shown, important e.g. for low bridges.

zeichen-86.question: What does this traffic sign with a length value mean?

zeichen-87.question: You are driving on a fast road and see this traffic sign. What must you observe?

options.a: Turning around is allowed if no traffic is coming.
options.b: Turning left is prohibited.
options.c: Turning around (U-turn) is prohibited on this stretch of road.
options.d: Reversing is prohibited.

zeichen-87.explanation: Sign 272 prohibits U-turns. On fast roads a U-turn manoeuvre is especially dangerous, which is why this prohibition is strictly imposed and enforced there.

zeichen-88.question: You are driving a truck and see this traffic sign showing 70m. What must you observe?

options.a: The gap to the vehicle behind you must be at most 70m.
options.b: You must keep a minimum following distance of 70m to the vehicle ahead.
options.c: The maximum permitted speed here is 70 km/h.
options.d: The next rest area is 70m away.

zeichen-88.explanation: Sign 273 requires motor vehicles over 3.5t to keep a minimum following distance to the vehicle ahead, to avoid rear-end collisions if it brakes suddenly.

zeichen-89.question: What does this blue traffic sign with the bus symbol mark, for example at a school bus stop?

options.a: A stop for scheduled buses/trams, where other vehicles may not stop.
options.b: A ban on buses.
options.c: A bus-only lane.
options.d: A taxi rank.

zeichen-89.explanation: Sign 224 marks stops for trams or scheduled buses (including school buses); other vehicles may not stop in the stop area.

zeichen-90.question: What does this traffic sign with the wording TAXI mean?

options.a: Taxis are prohibited here.
options.b: Taxi rank - this space is reserved for waiting taxis.
options.c: Mandatory direction of travel for taxis.
options.d: End of the taxi rank.

zeichen-90.explanation: Sign 229 marks a taxi rank; other vehicles generally may not park there.

zeichen-91.question: What does this traffic sign with a bicycle and pedestrian symbol, divided by a line, mean?

options.a: A shared footpath and cycle path - both use the same surface.
options.b: Cycle path, pedestrians prohibited.
options.c: Separated bicycle and footpath - each stays on their own side.
options.d: Pedestrian zone, cycling permitted.

zeichen-91.explanation: Sign 241 marks a path with separate areas for cyclists and pedestrians; the dividing line may not be crossed.

zeichen-92.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.a: Start of a pedestrian zone.
options.b: End of a pedestrian zone.
options.c: Mandatory footpath.
options.d: No pedestrians.

zeichen-92.explanation: Sign 242.1 marks the start of a pedestrian zone; vehicle traffic there is generally only permitted in exceptional cases.

zeichen-93.question: What does this traffic sign with the crossed-out pedestrian symbol mean?

options.a: Start of a pedestrian zone.
options.b: End of a pedestrian zone.
options.c: No pedestrians.
options.d: Footpath damaged.

zeichen-93.explanation: Sign 242.2 marks the end of a pedestrian zone; from here on the general traffic rules apply again.

zeichen-94.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.a: Start of a bicycle street.
options.b: End of a bicycle street.
options.c: Mandatory cycle path.
options.d: No cyclists.

zeichen-94.explanation: Sign 244.1 marks the start of a bicycle street; motor vehicle traffic is only exceptionally permitted there and cyclists have priority.

zeichen-95.question: What does this traffic sign with the crossed-out bicycle symbol mean?

options.a: Start of a bicycle street.
options.b: End of a bicycle street.
options.c: No cyclists.
options.d: Cycle path damaged.

zeichen-95.explanation: Sign 244.2 marks the end of a bicycle street.

zeichen-96.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.a: A stop for scheduled buses.
options.b: No buses.
options.c: Bus-only lane - reserved for scheduled buses (and any explicitly permitted vehicles).
options.d: A taxi rank.

zeichen-96.explanation: Sign 245 marks a special lane that may only be used by scheduled buses (and any vehicles explicitly permitted by a supplementary plate).

zeichen-97.question: You drive into a zone marked with this traffic sign. What applies there?

options.a: A restricted no-stopping rule applies throughout the whole zone.
options.b: Only at this exact spot does no-stopping apply, otherwise stopping is allowed in the zone.
options.c: No-parking applies in the zone, but stopping is allowed.
options.d: The zone may only be entered by residents.

zeichen-97.explanation: Sign 290.1 marks the start of a zone with restricted no-stopping; the rule applies until the corresponding end sign (290.2), not just at the sign's location.

zeichen-98.question: What does this traffic sign (with the extra grey diagonal line) mean?

options.a: Start of a restricted no-stopping zone.
options.b: End of the restricted no-stopping zone.
options.c: Start of an absolute no-stopping restriction.
options.d: The no-stopping zone now only applies to trucks.

zeichen-98.explanation: Sign 290.2 marks the end of the restricted no-stopping zone; from here on the general stopping and parking rules apply again.

zeichen-99.question: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.a: An ordinary parking area with no special purpose.
options.b: A park-and-ride facility for switching to bus or train.
options.c: A parking ban near a railway station.
options.d: A parking area reserved only for coaches.

zeichen-99.explanation: Sign 316 marks a Park & Ride facility, where drivers can switch to public transport.

zeichen-100.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.d: A parking area open only in summer.

zeichen-100.explanation: Sign 317 marks a hikers' parking area, where vehicles can be left before setting off on a hike.

zeichen-101.question: What applies from this traffic sign onward?

options.d: A parking area reserved for residents only.

zeichen-101.explanation: Sign 325.1 marks the start of a traffic-calmed area, where walking pace applies and pedestrians may use the entire width of the area.

zeichen-102.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.a: The start of a traffic-calmed area.
options.b: The start of a pedestrian zone.
options.c: A notice that a traffic-calmed area begins in 100 metres.
options.d: The end of a traffic-calmed area.

zeichen-102.explanation: Sign 325.2 marks the end of a traffic-calmed area; ordinary traffic rules apply again from this point.

zeichen-103.question: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.a: An underpass for pedestrians only.
options.b: The start of a tunnel.
options.c: A bridge with a height restriction.
options.d: A narrowing of the road.

zeichen-103.explanation: Sign 327 marks the start of a tunnel.

zeichen-104.question: What applies from this traffic sign onward?

options.a: The start of a motorway (Autobahn).
options.b: A general ban on motor vehicles.
options.c: The start of a motor-vehicle-only road, which may only be used by motor vehicles.
options.d: The end of a speed limit.

zeichen-104.explanation: Sign 331.1 marks the start of a motor-vehicle-only road; only motor vehicles may use it, but it is not a motorway.

zeichen-105.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.a: The start of a motor-vehicle-only road.
options.b: The end of a motor-vehicle-only road.
options.c: The end of a motorway.
options.d: An overtaking ban for motor vehicles.

zeichen-105.explanation: Sign 331.2 marks the end of the motor-vehicle-only road; ordinary rules for the road apply again from this point.

zeichen-106.question: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.a: The start of a water protection area.
options.b: A ferry connection.
options.c: A flood-risk area.
options.d: A car wash at the next exit.

zeichen-106.explanation: Sign 354 marks the start of a water protection area, where special care is required, e.g. regarding substances that could contaminate water.

zeichen-107.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.a: A pedestrian crossing with traffic lights.
options.b: A ban on stopping near a school.
options.c: The location of a crossing guard who helps pedestrians, e.g. schoolchildren, cross the road.
options.d: A ban on carrying children in the vehicle.

zeichen-107.explanation: Sign 356 marks the location of a crossing guard, who in particular helps schoolchildren cross the road safely.

zeichen-108.question: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.a: A pharmacy.
options.b: A first-aid station.
options.c: A hospital with an emergency department.
options.d: A rescue helicopter landing site.

zeichen-109.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.a: A speed-camera enforcement zone.
options.b: A fire station.
options.c: A courthouse.
options.d: A police station.

zeichen-110.question: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.a: A motorway service area with a restaurant.
options.b: A truck parking area with no further facilities.
options.c: A truck stop (Autohof) with fuel and overnight accommodation.
options.d: A vehicle repair workshop.

zeichen-110.explanation: Sign 448.1 indicates a truck stop (Autohof), which offers fuel, overnight accommodation, and other services for drivers.

zeichen-111.question: What does this information sign indicate?

options.b: An EV charging station.
options.c: A car wash.
options.d: A tyre repair shop.

zeichen-111.explanation: The information sign, showing a fuel pump symbol, indicates a fuel station.

zeichen-112.question: What does this information sign indicate?

options.c: A campsite.
options.d: A police station.

zeichen-112.explanation: The cutlery symbol on this information sign indicates a rest area offering food.

zeichen-113.question: What does this information sign indicate?

options.a: A restaurant with a phone booth.
options.b: An EV charging station.
options.c: An emergency call point or telephone.
options.d: A police station.

zeichen-113.explanation: The information sign, showing a handset symbol, indicates an emergency call point or telephone.

zeichen-114.question: What does this information sign indicate?

options.d: A campsite.

zeichen-114.explanation: The tent symbol on this information sign indicates a campsite.

zeichen-115.question: What does this information sign indicate?

options.d: A nearby power outage.

zeichen-115.explanation: The plug symbol on this information sign indicates an EV charging station.

zeichen-116.question: What does this information sign indicate?

options.a: A shower for travellers.
options.b: A public restroom.
options.c: A changing room.
options.d: A kiosk.

zeichen-116.explanation: The information sign, showing figure symbols, indicates a public restroom.

zeichen-117.question: What does this traffic sign indicate?

zeichen-117.explanation: Sign 328 marks an emergency stopping and breakdown bay, where vehicles can stop in case of a breakdown or emergency.

zeichen-118.question: What does this yellow town-name sign mean?

zeichen-119.question: What does this town-name sign with the crossed-out name mean?

zeichen-120.question: What does this yellow numbered plate indicate?

options.d: The distance to the next town in kilometres.

zeichen-120.explanation: Sign 401 shows the number of a federal road (Bundesstraße), e.g. B 1, in black text on a yellow plate.

zeichen-121.question: What does this green plate with white lettering indicate?

options.b: The number of a motorway (Autobahn).
options.c: A green low-emission zone.
options.d: The number of a European route (Europastraße).

zeichen-122.question: What is this yellow, pointed direction sign?

zeichen-123.question: What is this blue, pointed direction sign?

options.c: A no-stopping sign.
options.d: A signpost to the next rest area.

zeichen-123.explanation: Sign 430, with a blue background and white lettering, shows the way to the motorway.

zeichen-124.question: What does this white sign with black text show?

options.a: The number of a federal road.
options.b: The house numbers of the adjoining buildings.
options.c: The name of the street.
options.d: A recommended speed.

zeichen-124.explanation: Sign 437 is the street name sign and shows the name of the street.

zeichen-125.question: What does this white plate with several town names and numbers show?

options.a: The order of the next exits.
options.b: A speed limit that depends on the town.
options.c: A warning about several hazard locations.
options.d: A distance table showing distances to several towns.

zeichen-125.explanation: Sign 453 is a distance table, showing distances to several towns along the route.

zeichen-126.question: A white supplementary plate with a black directional arrow is mounted below a traffic sign. What does this plate mean?

options.a: The sign above applies only to the direction/area indicated by the arrow.
options.b: Traffic must be diverted in the direction of the arrow.
options.c: The road becomes one-way in the direction shown.
options.d: The supplementary sign applies to the whole stretch regardless of the arrow direction.

zeichen-126.explanation: The directional-arrow plate (No. 1000) specifies that the sign above it applies to the direction or stretch of road indicated by the arrow.

zeichen-127.question: A white supplementary plate reading ‘300 m’ is mounted below a danger sign. What does it mean?

options.a: It marks a 300-metre speed-limit zone.
options.b: It states the distance to where the hazard/rule shown above begins, or how far it still applies.
options.c: The next parking area is 300 metres away.
options.d: It is 300 metres to the town boundary from this point.

zeichen-127.explanation: The distance plate (No. 1001) states the distance to where the hazard or rule of the sign above it starts, or how far it continues.

zeichen-128.question: Below the priority-road sign is a plate showing a bent thick line. What does this plate indicate?

options.a: The priority road ends at this junction.
options.b: This is a dead end.
options.c: The course/shape the priority road takes through the upcoming junction.
options.d: Give way to vehicles turning in from the right.

zeichen-128.explanation: Sign No. 1002 schematically shows how the priority road runs through an upcoming junction, so road users know where the right of way continues.

zeichen-129.question: Below a general danger sign, a plate shows a caravan with skid lines. Who does this plate specifically warn?

options.a: Vehicles towing a caravan, since car-caravan combinations face an increased risk of skidding here.
options.b: Only motorhomes without a trailer.
options.c: Pedestrians carrying luggage.
options.d: Vehicles intending to overtake a caravan.

zeichen-129.explanation: Sign No. 1006 indicates that the hazard shown on the sign above particularly affects vehicles towing a caravan, e.g. at locations with an increased skidding risk for such combinations.

zeichen-130.question: A white supplementary plate reading ‘Radfahrer frei’ (cyclists exempted) is mounted below a prohibition sign. What does it mean?

options.a: Cyclists must dismount here.
options.b: The prohibition of the main sign does not apply to cyclists, they may still use that stretch.
options.c: Only racing cyclists may use it, other cyclists may not.
options.d: Cyclists have right of way over all other road users here.

zeichen-130.explanation: A plate reading ‘Radfahrer frei’ exempts cyclists from a prohibition that otherwise applies to all other vehicles – they may continue to use that stretch of road.

zeichen-131.question: A supplementary plate below a prohibition sign reads ‘Anlieger frei’ (residents/local traffic exempted). Who may still proceed despite the prohibition?

options.a: Only people who live there, have a destination there, or business to conduct there (local origin/destination traffic).
options.b: Everyone – the prohibition effectively no longer applies.
options.c: Only parcel delivery vehicles.
options.d: Only vehicles with an official special permit.

zeichen-131.explanation: ‘Anlieger frei’ exempts local origin-and-destination traffic (residents, visitors, deliveries with an actual destination there) from the prohibition; through-traffic remains prohibited.

zeichen-132.question: A white supplementary sign reading "Fußgänger" (pedestrians) is attached below a traffic sign. What does that mean?

options.a: The supplementary sign indicates that the main sign's rule also applies to pedestrians.
options.b: Pedestrians are generally exempt from whatever the main sign regulates.
options.c: It's an indication of a pedestrian zone nearby.
options.d: The supplementary sign only applies to wheelchair users, not other pedestrians.

zeichen-132.explanation: The supplementary sign 1010-53 "Fußgänger" clarifies the scope of the main sign above it: it makes clear the rule also includes pedestrians, rather than applying only to vehicles as might otherwise be assumed.

zeichen-133.question: A supplementary plate shows a bicycle symbol with a diagonal line, mounted below another traffic sign. What does it mean?

options.a: Cyclists may no longer use the road from this point on.
options.b: The cycle path ends at this point; the sign above relates to the end of the cycle path.
options.c: A speed limit applies only to cyclists from here.
options.d: Cyclists must ride on the carriageway from here, but this is optional.

zeichen-133.explanation: Sign No. 1012-31 marks the end of a cycle path; it is mounted below the relevant main sign to alert cyclists that the separate cycle path is ending.

zeichen-134.question: A supplementary plate below a sign shows a bicycle next to a walking figure (‘Radfahrer absteigen’ – cyclists dismount). What is expected of cyclists here?

options.a: They should dismount at this point and push their bicycle.
options.b: They may ride at any speed they like here.
options.c: They must leave their bicycle here and continue on foot.
options.d: They must move onto the carriageway and continue riding there.

zeichen-134.explanation: Sign No. 1012-32 ‘Radfahrer absteigen’ instructs cyclists to dismount and push their bicycle at that point, usually because of a narrow or unsafe stretch.

zeichen-135.question: A supplementary plate showing a wheelchair symbol is mounted below a no-parking sign. What does this plate mean?

options.a: The parking ban applies to all vehicles except wheelchairs.
options.b: This marks the entrance to a barrier-free building.
options.c: Anyone may park here as long as a wheelchair is carried in the vehicle.
options.d: The parking ban does not apply to vehicles of severely disabled persons holding the corresponding parking permit.

zeichen-135.explanation: Sign No. 1020-11 exempts holders of a severe-disability parking permit from a parking ban – it is a specific parking privilege, not a general exemption for everyone.

zeichen-136.question: A supplementary plate below a no-parking sign reads ‘mit Parkausweis Nr. ... frei’ (residents with permit no. ... exempted). Who may still park here?

options.a: Any resident of the town, regardless of holding a permit.
options.b: Only tradespeople and delivery vehicles with business nearby.
options.c: Only holders of the residents’ parking permit issued under the specified number.
options.d: Only vehicles with a valid disabled-parking permit.

zeichen-136.explanation: This plate exempts only holders of the residents' parking permit issued under the stated number, not residents in general and not holders of disability permits.

zeichen-137.question: A supplementary plate below a sign shows a crossed-out hard-shoulder symbol. What does this plate mean?

options.a: The hard shoulder is not usable, e.g. due to roadworks or damage, and must not be used.
options.b: A speed limit applies on the hard shoulder from this point.
options.c: The hard shoulder may only be used by bicycles.
options.d: Parking is permitted on the hard shoulder from this point.

zeichen-137.explanation: This plate indicates that the hard shoulder is not usable at that location, for example due to roadworks, damage, or other obstructions.

vorfahrt-26.question: You are driving on a priority road (Zeichen 306). At a following intersection there is no new Zeichen 306 sign, and no Zeichen 307 sign either. What applies to your right of way?

options.a: The priority road generally continues to the next intersection unless it was explicitly ended by Zeichen 307
options.b: The priority road automatically ends at any intersection where no sign is posted
options.c: Without a new sign, right-before-left applies immediately, regardless of the road's course
options.d: Priority ends as soon as the road makes a slight curve

vorfahrt-26.explanation: A once-signed priority road remains in effect until it is explicitly ended by Zeichen 307; it does not need to be re-announced at every intersection.

vorfahrt-27.question: You are driving through a roundabout where tram tracks cross the circulatory carriageway. A tram is approaching on these tracks. How do you behave?

options.a: You always have priority over the tram inside the roundabout
options.b: Because you are already circulating, the tram must always wait
options.c: The tram generally has priority; you must let it cross the roundabout carriageway
options.d: Whoever honks first may go first

vorfahrt-27.explanation: Rail vehicles generally have priority under §9 Abs. 3 StVO; this also applies where their tracks run through a roundabout.

vorfahrt-28.question: You turn right off a priority road into a side street. In doing so you cross a physically separated, continuous cycle path along which a cyclist is riding straight ahead. Who has right of way?

options.a: You, because you are on the higher-ranking road
options.b: The cyclist, because they are riding straight on along the cycle path in their direction of travel
options.c: Right-before-left applies between you and the cyclist
options.d: The cyclist must always stop when a car is turning

vorfahrt-28.explanation: A driver turning off must let straight-ahead cyclists on a crossing cycle path pass; the turn must not endanger the cyclist.

vorfahrt-29.question: The carriageway narrows to one lane because of roadworks. You face sign Zeichen 208 (give way to oncoming traffic). A vehicle is already coming through the narrow section from the opposite direction. What do you do?

options.a: You drive in briskly, since Zeichen 208 generally gives you priority
options.b: You honk so the oncoming vehicle reverses
options.c: You drive through the narrow section at the same time as the oncoming vehicle
options.d: You wait before the narrow section until the oncoming vehicle has passed through it

vorfahrt-29.explanation: Zeichen 208 requires you to give way to oncoming traffic that is already passing through and only enter the narrow section afterwards.

vorfahrt-30.question: On a narrow bridge with no traffic signs, two vehicles cannot safely pass each other. A vehicle is already on the bridge coming towards you. How do you behave?

options.a: You generally have priority because you reached the bridge first
options.b: You wait before the bridge until the oncoming vehicle has left it
options.c: Both vehicles slowly enter the bridge at the same time
options.d: The larger vehicle automatically has priority

vorfahrt-30.explanation: Without special signage, the general duty of mutual consideration in §6 StVO means the vehicle that has not yet entered the narrow point must wait to avoid danger.

vorfahrt-31.question: You are driving out of the exit of a shopping centre car park onto a normal street. How do you behave towards moving traffic on the street?

options.a: You have priority because you are coming from a signposted facility
options.b: Right-before-left applies because both areas are publicly accessible
options.c: You must behave as when leaving a property and must not endanger moving traffic
options.d: You may only enter if no other vehicle is in sight at all

vorfahrt-31.explanation: A car park is legally treated like private property; entering the street from it therefore falls under the special duty of care in §10 StVO, not right-before-left.

vorfahrt-32.question: You reach a T-junction with no traffic signs at all. Your road ends there, and the through road runs from left to right in front of you. A vehicle is approaching from the right on the through road. How do you behave?

options.a: You must give way to the vehicle from the right, regardless of the road layout
options.b: Because your road ends, you automatically have priority
options.c: The through road always has priority, even without signage
options.d: You may enter as soon as the other vehicle indicates

vorfahrt-32.explanation: Without traffic signs, right-before-left applies at any intersection or junction, including a T-junction; the physical road layout alone does not establish priority.

vorfahrt-33.question: You are stopped at a red light. From behind, an ambulance approaches with blue lights and siren, wanting to get through the intersection even though it also appears blocked for it. How do you behave?

options.a: You just stay stopped, since you may not drive on red anyway
options.b: You drive into the intersection on red to make room
options.c: You wait until the light turns green and then let the ambulance go first
options.d: You make way as far as safely possible, e.g. by pulling aside, but stay clear of the intersection until it is safe to proceed

vorfahrt-33.explanation: Emergency vehicles using blue lights and siren must be given way immediately, but this must not be done by dangerously entering a red-light intersection; it must be done only as far as it is safely possible.

vorfahrt-34.question: At a traffic light, the main signal shows a straight-ahead green, but there is no additional green arrow sign for right turns. You want to turn right on red. Is that allowed?

options.a: Yes, turning right on red is always generally allowed in Germany
options.b: Yes, as long as no pedestrian is crossing the road
options.c: No, without the separately mounted green arrow sign (Zeichen 720) you may not turn right on red
options.d: Yes, but only outside built-up areas

vorfahrt-34.explanation: Unlike in some other countries, turning right on red in Germany is only permitted with the separately mounted green arrow sign (Zeichen 720), not automatically.

vorfahrt-35.question: In a built-up area, a scheduled bus is at a stop with its indicator on, about to pull away. How do you behave as you approach on the road?

options.a: You continue at unreduced speed; the bus has to wait
options.b: You must let the bus pull out and, if necessary, reduce your speed so that you can stop if required
options.c: You may only pass the bus once it has fully entered the roadway
options.d: This bus priority only applies outside built-up areas

vorfahrt-35.explanation: Under §20 Abs. 5 StVO, vehicles must let scheduled buses that signal their departure from a stop within a built-up area pull out, waiting if necessary.

vorfahrt-36.question: At an intersection with no priority signs, a rider on a horse approaches from the right. How do you behave?

options.a: The rider has right of way from the right just like a vehicle driver; you must let them pass
options.b: Riders generally have no right of way over motor vehicles
options.c: You may go first because horses count as animals, not as road users
options.d: Whichever means of transport is faster has priority

vorfahrt-36.explanation: Riders count as vehicle drivers under the StVO and are subject to the same right-of-way rules as other vehicles, including right-before-left.

vorfahrt-37.question: At an intersection, a priority sign is missing because it was clearly knocked down or torn off, leaving only the empty post. How do you behave if you are not sure how the intersection is actually signed?

options.a: You continue at normal speed, since a missing sign does not create right of way
options.b: You automatically have priority because no sign is visible
options.c: You approach with particular caution, ready to brake, treating it as right-before-left if in doubt
options.d: You must come to a complete stop as if Zeichen 206 were present

vorfahrt-37.explanation: When signage is unclear or missing, the general duty of care requires extra caution; when in doubt, the basic right-before-left rule should be assumed until the actual arrangement becomes clear.

vorfahrt-38.question: You are reversing out of a private driveway onto the street. A pedestrian on the pavement you must cross is approaching. Who has priority?

options.a: You, because you are already reversing and cannot be expected to stop
options.b: The pedestrian has priority; you must wait until they have passed the pavement area
options.c: Right-before-left applies between you and the pedestrian
options.d: The pedestrian must stop as soon as they notice a vehicle

vorfahrt-38.explanation: Anyone driving from a property onto the street must let pedestrians on the pavement being crossed pass and must not endanger them - this applies regardless of direction of travel.

vorfahrt-39.question: On a narrow lane next to a building, a fire truck with blue lights on is reversing to reach an incident, while a spotter is directing traffic. How do you behave?

options.a: You continue normally, since reversing generally does not establish right of way
options.b: You have priority because reversing vehicles must always wait
options.c: You ignore the spotter if you were at the location first
options.d: You follow the spotter's instructions and give way to the fire truck so as not to hinder the operation

vorfahrt-39.explanation: Emergency vehicles using blue lights have the right of way and must not be obstructed during an operational drive, including while reversing with a spotter; the spotter's instructions must be followed.

vorfahrt-40.question: You are approaching a level crossing with half-barriers, which are already lowering while a gap still remains at the edge of the road. How do you behave?

options.a: You drive briskly through the gap as long as the barrier has not yet reached the middle of the road
options.b: You may drive through as long as no train is visible
options.c: You stop in good time before the level crossing as soon as the barriers begin to lower
options.d: Half-barriers only apply to pedestrians, not to vehicles

vorfahrt-40.explanation: Lowering barriers, including half-barriers, indicate an approaching train; vehicles must stop in good time before the crossing and must not drive through any remaining gap.

vorfahrt-41.question: Immediately before a confusing intersection, overtaking is prohibited by Zeichen 276. A vehicle required to yield at this intersection wants to turn into your street while you approach the intersection. What role does the overtaking ban play for the right-of-way situation?

options.a: The overtaking ban automatically also removes your right of way
options.b: The overtaking ban does not change the right-of-way rules; it only prevents dangerous overtaking near the intersection, your right of way remains
options.c: Vehicles required to yield may always enter first when there is an overtaking ban
options.d: You must exceptionally stop at this intersection because overtaking is prohibited

vorfahrt-41.explanation: An overtaking ban and the right-of-way rules are two independent regulations; the ban is a safety measure for overtaking and does not change who has priority at the intersection.

vorfahrt-42.question: At a roadworks site, the original right-of-way arrangement was changed by temporary, mobile signage that differs from the permanent signage. Which signage applies to you?

options.a: The currently installed temporary roadworks signage takes precedence over the permanent signage
options.b: The permanent signage always continues to apply; temporary roadworks signs are only recommendations
options.c: Both arrangements apply at the same time, whichever is more favourable to you
options.d: Right-before-left automatically applies whenever signage is contradictory

vorfahrt-42.explanation: Temporary roadworks signage is specifically installed to adapt traffic flow to the changed situation, and it takes precedence over contradicting permanent signage.

vorfahrt-43.question: At a signalised intersection your light shows green, while at the same time a tram on separate tracks, for which no dedicated signal is visible, is approaching and also entering the intersection. How do you behave?

options.a: Your green light always has priority over the tram
options.b: You must stop because rail vehicles may generally ignore traffic lights
options.c: You let the tram pass despite your green light if it has already visibly entered the intersection, in order to avoid a collision
options.d: Signal signs strictly override each other; the traffic light alone decides

vorfahrt-43.explanation: Rail vehicles generally have priority; even if a traffic light shows green for road traffic without a separate signal for the tram, any recognisable risk of collision must still be avoided by stopping.

gefahr-26.question: Which factor on your vehicle most increases the risk of hydroplaning in the rain?

options.a: A heavy load in the boot
options.b: Insufficient tire tread depth
options.c: A full fuel tank
options.d: A low seat position

gefahr-26.explanation: Worn tires can no longer channel water away effectively. This lets a water film build up between tire and road faster, causing loss of road contact.

gefahr-27.question: You are driving on the motorway in dense fog and can only see about 50 metres ahead. How should you behave?

options.a: Follow closely so you keep the vehicle ahead's tail lights in view
options.b: Keep your speed but switch on the hazard lights
options.c: Reduce speed significantly and increase the distance to the vehicle ahead
options.d: Only switch on high beam so you can see further

gefahr-27.explanation: In heavily reduced visibility, speed must be adjusted so you can stop within your sight distance. A larger gap gives extra reaction time. High beam actually worsens visibility in fog because it reflects off the droplets.

gefahr-28.question: Why does black ice form especially early on bridges when frost sets in, even while the rest of the road is still ice-free?

options.a: Bridges cool from above and below at the same time because air circulates underneath them
options.b: Bridges generally receive less road salt than a normal carriageway
options.c: Bridges are made of asphalt, which freezes faster than concrete
options.d: Heat from vehicles builds up more strongly on bridges than elsewhere

gefahr-28.explanation: Unlike a normal road surface, which is warmed from below by the ground, a bridge is exposed to air on both sides. It loses heat from above and below, so it cools below freezing point faster.

gefahr-29.question: At what time of day is the risk of being strongly dazzled by low sun especially high for drivers heading east-west?

options.a: Only around midday
options.b: Only under cloudy skies
options.c: Only in summer when the sun is high
options.d: Shortly after sunrise and shortly before sunset

gefahr-29.explanation: When the sun is low on the horizon, its light hits the driver's eyes almost horizontally when driving directly toward sunrise or sunset. This causes severe glare.

gefahr-30.question: Which sign is an early indicator that you are getting tired and should take a break?

options.a: You automatically drive slower than the speed limit
options.b: You notice you are blinking more often and your eyes feel heavy
options.c: You turn up the music to stay awake
options.d: You suddenly feel more alert and automatically drive faster

gefahr-30.explanation: More frequent blinking, heavy eyelids and blurring vision are typical early fatigue signs. Ignoring them risks microsleep, so a break is urgently needed.

gefahr-31.question: Why is operating a touchscreen infotainment system while driving more dangerous than using a simple rotary knob?

options.a: Touchscreens use more power than rotary knobs
options.b: A touchscreen can be operated just as blindly, by feel, as a rotary knob
options.c: A touchscreen requires looking longer because menus must be read visually
options.d: Touchscreens are legally only allowed while the vehicle is stationary

gefahr-31.explanation: A rotary knob can often be operated by feel without looking. A touchscreen requires the eyes to read the menu, taking the gaze off the road for longer and increasing accident risk.

gefahr-32.question: You are driving on a rural road past unfenced pastureland. What must you watch out for in particular?

options.a: Grazing animals such as sheep or cattle can suddenly step onto the road
options.b: A 30 km/h limit automatically applies next to pastureland
options.c: Overtaking is generally prohibited there
options.d: By law, grazing animals always stay at least 5 metres from the road

gefahr-32.explanation: Without a fence, grazing animals can step onto the road at any time. Drivers must choose a speed that allows them to stop in time if an animal suddenly appears.

gefahr-33.question: You are driving past a primary school around 1 pm while children are leaving the premises. How should you behave?

options.a: Continue driving normally, since children are responsible for their own safety
options.b: Only slow down if a 'School' sign has been put up
options.c: Sound the horn so the children step back in time
options.d: Significantly reduce speed and be ready to brake at any time

gefahr-33.explanation: Children often cannot reliably judge road traffic and may run onto the road suddenly. Extra caution is required near schools at pickup times, regardless of signage.

gefahr-34.question: Why is an unpaved gravel road especially demanding for vehicle handling?

options.a: Because a minimum speed of 60 km/h is generally required there
options.b: Because loose stones reduce grip, and abrupt steering or braking can make the vehicle skid
options.c: Because gravel roads are approved for bicycles only
options.d: Because headlights must be switched off there

gefahr-34.explanation: Loose gravel offers tires much less grip than solid asphalt. Sudden steering or braking movements can therefore easily cause the vehicle to skid or slide out.

gefahr-35.question: You are driving at high speed across an exposed, elevated bridge in strong crosswind. What is the biggest danger?

options.a: The engine can overheat because of the wind
options.b: The brakes lose effectiveness because of the wind
options.c: The vehicle can be pushed sideways out of its lane, especially when leaving a sheltered section
options.d: Fuel consumption drops dangerously fast

gefahr-35.explanation: Strong crosswind on exposed, elevated stretches can push the vehicle sideways. The transition from a sheltered spot to an open one is especially critical, because the gust hits suddenly.

gefahr-36.question: Why should you adjust your speed at night on rural roads to the range of your dipped headlights?

options.a: Because only then can you stop in time within the illuminated distance
options.b: Because police carry out stricter checks at night
options.c: Because dipped headlights automatically switch off at too high a speed
options.d: Because a different general speed limit applies at night

gefahr-36.explanation: Dipped headlights illuminate the road only over a limited distance. Driving faster than you could stop within that visible range risks spotting an obstacle too late.

gefahr-37.question: Why should you pay particular attention to keeping enough distance from the vehicle ahead in a tunnel?

options.a: Because headlights are generally not allowed in tunnels
options.b: Because in the event of a rear-end crash in a tunnel, rescue and escape are much harder
options.c: Because tunnels always have an uphill gradient that lengthens braking distance
options.d: Because rear fog lights may not be used in tunnels

gefahr-37.explanation: In a tunnel, smoke from an accident is especially dangerous, and rescuers and fleeing people have fewer escape routes. Keeping enough distance reduces the risk of a rear-end crash in the first place.

gefahr-38.question: The driver ahead of you suddenly brakes hard for no apparent reason. What best protects you from rear-ending them?

options.a: Keeping the smallest possible gap so you can react faster
options.b: Constantly watching the interior mirror instead of the road ahead
options.c: Immediately swerving into the oncoming lane
options.d: An adequate safety distance that leaves you room for reaction and braking distance

gefahr-38.explanation: An adequate following distance is the most effective protection against rear-end crashes because it covers both reaction time and braking distance. Too small a gap leaves no time to react to unexpected braking.

gefahr-39.question: You are taking a prescription medication whose leaflet warns of drowsiness and slowed reaction time. What should you do before driving?

options.a: Simply drive more carefully than usual, that is enough
options.b: Ignore the effect as long as no alcohol was consumed
options.c: Check beforehand whether your fitness to drive is impaired, and refrain from driving if necessary
options.d: Only pay attention to the effect on trips over 100 km

gefahr-39.explanation: Even legal, prescription medication can significantly impair fitness to drive, for example through drowsiness or slowed reaction. Anyone impaired must refrain from driving, regardless of alcohol.

gefahr-40.question: You are driving a fully loaded vehicle down a long, steep downhill stretch. Why should you shift into a lower gear in good time instead of relying only on the brakes?

options.a: Because a low gear reduces fuel consumption and that is the only purpose
options.b: Because continuous braking under heavy load can overheat the brakes and reduce their effectiveness
options.c: Because regulations forbid using the brakes on downhill stretches
options.d: Because a low gear automatically makes the vehicle lighter

gefahr-40.explanation: Long, heavily loaded braking can overheat the brake system so much that braking power drops ('brake fade'). A low gear uses engine braking and relieves the service brakes.

umwelt-26.question: When should you check your tyre pressure to get an accurate reading?

options.a: Right after a longer motorway journey
options.b: When the tyres are cold, i.e. before starting the trip
options.c: Only immediately after washing the vehicle
options.d: It does not matter when you measure it

umwelt-26.explanation: Driving heats up the air inside the tyre, which raises the measured pressure. Only a measurement on cold tyres shows the actual value the vehicle specification is based on.

umwelt-27.question: Besides fuel efficiency, what else does the EU tyre label show?

options.a: Only the tyre's month of manufacture
options.b: Wet grip (braking performance in the wet) and external rolling noise
options.c: Only the maximum lifespan in kilometres
options.d: The recommended rim colour

umwelt-27.explanation: The EU tyre label rates fuel efficiency (rolling resistance), wet grip and external rolling noise, so buyers can compare tyres.

umwelt-28.question: How can you tell that your vehicle's brake pads are worn?

options.a: Persistent squealing when braking or a warning indicator on the dashboard
options.b: The fuel filler cap becomes harder to open
options.c: The horn becomes noticeably quieter
options.d: The windscreen wipers work more slowly

umwelt-28.explanation: Many vehicles have wear indicators on the brake pads that produce a squealing sound or trigger a warning light once the pad thickness drops below a minimum limit.

umwelt-29.question: What is the function of the catalytic converter in the exhaust system of a petrol-engine vehicle?

options.a: It directly reduces fuel consumption
options.b: It converts harmful exhaust components into less harmful substances
options.c: It cools the engine under high load
options.d: It filters particulate matter out of the exhaust

umwelt-29.explanation: Through chemical reactions, the catalytic converter transforms exhaust components such as carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides into less harmful substances like water and carbon dioxide.

umwelt-30.question: What is the main function of the particulate filter in a diesel vehicle?

options.a: It filters water out of the fuel
options.b: It reduces the engine's noise level
options.c: It retains solid soot particles from the exhaust
options.d: It cools the engine oil

umwelt-30.explanation: The particulate filter captures fine soot particles from a diesel engine's exhaust stream so this health-damaging particulate matter does not enter the air unfiltered.

umwelt-31.question: How do you drive an electric vehicle in a particularly energy-efficient way?

options.a: Drive with foresight and lift off the accelerator early to use regenerative braking to recover energy
options.b: Brake as late and hard as possible to preserve the brake lights
options.c: Always accelerate in the highest gear
options.d: Keep the air conditioning running at maximum constantly

umwelt-31.explanation: Lifting off the accelerator early lets the vehicle feed kinetic energy back into the battery through regenerative braking, instead of wasting it as heat during braking.

umwelt-32.question: Why is it important to use the engine oil type and viscosity specified by the manufacturer when topping up?

options.a: Only these oil types match the vehicle's paint colour
options.b: Other oil types are generally prohibited by law
options.c: It only affects the smell of the oil
options.d: Wrong oil can impair lubrication and engine protection and damage the engine

umwelt-32.explanation: Engine oils differ in viscosity and composition. Unsuitable oil can reduce lubrication performance and lead to increased wear or engine damage.

umwelt-33.question: Before starting your journey you notice that the windscreen washer reservoir is almost empty. What should you do?

options.a: It does not matter, since the wipers work fine dry
options.b: Fill the reservoir, since enough washer fluid is important for clear visibility
options.c: The fill level only matters when it rains
options.d: An empty reservoir has no effect on road safety

umwelt-33.explanation: Dirty windows are hard to clean without washer fluid, and dry wiping can scratch the glass. Clear visibility is essential for safe driving.

umwelt-34.question: You want to jump-start a vehicle with a dead battery using jump leads. What is especially important for safety?

options.a: Both engines must remain switched off during the entire procedure
options.b: The cables may be connected in any order
options.c: The correct order for connecting the terminals must be followed exactly, avoiding a short circuit
options.d: It is enough to connect only the negative terminals of both vehicles

umwelt-34.explanation: When jump-starting, the cables must be connected to the positive and negative terminals in a specific order. Doing it wrong can cause a short circuit, sparking, or even a battery explosion.

umwelt-35.question: How can cruise control usefully help save fuel?

options.a: On flat, lightly trafficked roads it keeps speed steady and avoids unnecessary acceleration
options.b: It should generally be used in dense city traffic
options.c: It completely replaces the driver's attention
options.d: It always increases consumption regardless of the road

umwelt-35.explanation: On even roads without much traffic, cruise control keeps speed constant and prevents frequent accelerating and braking, which saves fuel.

umwelt-36.question: Why should tyres be regularly rotated between the front and rear axle?

options.a: So that all tyres keep the same colour
options.b: To achieve more even wear on all tyres and extend their service life
options.c: Because tyres are prohibited on the rear axle
options.d: So that the speedometer stays correctly calibrated

umwelt-36.explanation: Depending on drivetrain and driving style, front and rear tyres wear differently. Regular rotation results in more even wear and a longer service life.

umwelt-37.question: What is checked during the exhaust emissions inspection (AU) as part of the general vehicle inspection?

options.a: Only the quality of the vehicle's paintwork
options.b: Only the condition of the seat covers
options.c: Whether the vehicle's exhaust emission values meet the prescribed limits
options.d: The volume of the car radio

umwelt-37.explanation: The exhaust emissions inspection determines whether the vehicle's emission values are within the permitted limits. It is part of the regular general inspection.

umwelt-38.question: Why should you check that your indicators and brake lights work before a longer trip?

options.a: Other road users can only recognise your driving intentions in time if the lights work correctly
options.b: This check is only necessary in fog
options.c: Indicators and brake lights have no effect on road safety
options.d: It is enough to have the lights checked once a year at the general inspection

umwelt-38.explanation: Working indicators and brake lights are important so that other road users can recognise a change of direction or braking in time and react accordingly.

umwelt-39.question: How does keeping a sufficient following distance to the vehicle ahead affect fuel consumption?

options.a: A larger distance always increases consumption
options.b: Distance has no effect on consumption whatsoever
options.c: Only speed affects consumption, distance is irrelevant
options.d: A sufficient distance allows foresighted driving with less abrupt braking and accelerating, which saves fuel

umwelt-39.explanation: Keeping enough distance lets you better anticipate traffic and reduces the need for hard braking followed by re-accelerating, which saves fuel and spares the brakes.

umwelt-40.question: What is the advantage of installing a child seat with ISOFIX mounting compared to securing it only with the vehicle seatbelt?

options.a: ISOFIX makes the child seat's own harness unnecessary
options.b: The child seat is connected directly and firmly to the car body via fixed anchor points, reducing the risk of installation errors
options.c: ISOFIX child seats may only be mounted on the front passenger seat
options.d: An ISOFIX child seat never needs an additional support leg or top tether

umwelt-40.explanation: ISOFIX connects the child seat firmly to the vehicle body via standardised anchor points. This reduces installation errors, which can occur more often with belt-only mounting.

verhalten-26.question: You are stopped in a traffic jam with the engine still running. May you pick up your phone briefly to read a message?

options.a: Yes, the phone ban does not apply in traffic jams
options.b: Yes, it is always allowed whenever the vehicle is stationary
options.c: No, as long as the engine is running the ban still applies while stopped in traffic
options.d: Yes, but only for a maximum of ten seconds

verhalten-26.explanation: The phone-use ban applies whenever the engine is running. The phone may only be used once the engine is switched off, for example during a longer standstill in a jam.

verhalten-27.question: When must you signal before changing lanes?

options.a: Only if other vehicles are nearby
options.b: In good time before every lane change, so others can react accordingly
options.c: Only at night or in poor visibility
options.d: Only on the motorway, not needed within town limits

verhalten-27.explanation: Anyone changing lanes must clearly signal in good time beforehand, regardless of whether other traffic is currently visible.

verhalten-28.question: Your wiper blades are badly worn and smear the windscreen in the rain. What is the correct response?

options.a: You must not continue driving like this, as road safety is no longer ensured
options.b: It does not matter as long as the wipers still move
options.c: You may continue if you drive more slowly
options.d: This only matters for the periodic vehicle inspection, not for the current trip

verhalten-28.explanation: The driver is responsible for the vehicle being roadworthy. Smeared visibility from worn wipers is a serious safety hazard and must not be accepted.

verhalten-29.question: You park at the side of the road and want to get out. What must you pay special attention to?

options.a: Only that the handbrake is applied
options.b: It is enough if the passenger keeps a lookout
options.c: A quick glance forward is sufficient
options.d: Before opening the door you must make sure no one is endangered, for example by checking over your shoulder

verhalten-29.explanation: When getting in or out, the driver must act so that other road users are not endangered. Looking over the shoulder before opening the door protects cyclists and pedestrians in particular.

verhalten-30.question: You want to overtake a cyclist on a narrow street. What must you observe?

options.a: Overtaking is always forbidden whenever a cyclist is present
options.b: You must keep sufficient lateral clearance and may only overtake if that clearance can be maintained
options.c: It is enough to briefly sound the horn and then overtake
options.d: Lateral clearance only matters outside built-up areas
