verhalten-30.explanation: A sufficient lateral clearance is required when overtaking cyclists, at least 1.5 metres within built-up areas. If a narrow street does not allow this clearance, overtaking is not permitted.

verhalten-31.question: A person in a wheelchair wants to cross the road at a pedestrian crossing without traffic lights. How must you behave as a driver?

options.a: You do not need to stop, since wheelchair users are not classed as pedestrians
options.b: You may pass at a reduced speed
options.c: You must allow them to cross and wait if necessary
options.d: This only applies to people using a white cane

verhalten-31.explanation: At pedestrian crossings, pedestrians, which includes wheelchair users, must be allowed to cross. Vehicles must wait if necessary.

verhalten-32.question: An ambulance is stopped at the roadside with its blue lights on, and paramedics are treating a person. How should you behave when passing?

options.a: You pass at clearly reduced speed and with as much lateral clearance as possible
options.b: You must always stop completely until the operation is finished
options.c: The blue light alone has no relevance for passing traffic
options.d: You may drive past normally as long as the siren is not sounding

verhalten-32.explanation: The general duty of care requires drivers to pass emergency scenes at reduced speed with sufficient clearance, so as not to endanger rescuers or the person being treated.

verhalten-33.question: Another vehicle is tailgating you closely and repeatedly flashes its headlights. What is the correct response?

options.a: Brake sharply and briefly to startle the tailgater
options.b: Keep calm, hold your speed, and move over safely to the right at the next safe opportunity to let them pass
options.c: Accelerate significantly to increase the gap
options.d: Ignore it completely and stay unchanged in the left lane

verhalten-33.explanation: You should never respond to tailgating with sudden braking (crash risk) - stay calm and change lane or make room safely at the next opportunity instead.

verhalten-34.question: You are driving with a small child who must be secured in a mandatory child seat. What else must you pay attention to?

options.a: The child seat only needs to be used on longer journeys
options.b: It is enough for the child to be buckled in with the normal seatbelt
options.c: The child seat must be age-appropriate and correctly installed for the protection to be effective
options.d: Child seats are only mandatory in the back seat, the seatbelt is enough in the front

verhalten-34.explanation: A child seat only provides protection if it matches the child's size and weight and is correctly installed. A seat that is merely present but wrongly used does not fulfil its purpose.

verhalten-35.question: You are towing a trailer and have to stop on the motorway hard shoulder due to a breakdown. What should you additionally do besides placing the warning triangle?

options.a: Nothing, the warning triangle alone is always sufficient
options.b: The hazard warning lights should be switched on as long as the vehicle poses a danger to others
options.c: Hazard warning lights must not be used while towing a trailer
options.d: It is sufficient to leave one turn indicator on continuously

verhalten-35.explanation: A broken-down vehicle that poses a danger to traffic must additionally be made visible with the hazard warning lights switched on for as long as the danger exists.

verhalten-36.question: Your vehicle breaks down in the middle of a tunnel. How do you behave?

options.a: You stay seated in the vehicle and wait for help
options.b: You stand behind your vehicle to make it more visible
options.c: You switch off all lights so as not to dazzle others
options.d: You switch on the hazard warning lights, leave the vehicle and move behind the barrier or to an emergency exit

verhalten-36.explanation: In a tunnel there is heightened danger from following traffic. After securing the vehicle with hazard lights, occupants should move to safety, for example behind protective barriers or to emergency exits.

verhalten-37.question: You encounter a funeral procession crossing the road. How do you behave?

options.a: You let the procession cross the road unhindered and wait
options.b: You may continue driving if you go slowly enough
options.c: Only the police may make a funeral procession stop
options.d: A funeral procession has no special priority over vehicles

verhalten-37.explanation: The general duty of mutual consideration means that an organised funeral procession must not be interrupted or held up; vehicles must wait until it has passed.

verhalten-38.question: It is broad daylight but raining heavily with reduced visibility. What applies to your vehicle's lighting?

options.a: Lighting is generally forbidden during daytime
options.b: When visibility is significantly reduced, dipped headlights must be switched on
options.c: The rear fog lamp and dipped headlights must always be used together
options.d: Switching on the parking lights is sufficient

verhalten-38.explanation: In fog, snowfall, rain or similar conditions with significantly reduced visibility, dipped headlights must be used even during daytime.

verhalten-39.question: You drive through a signed 30 km/h zone in front of a school. Is strictly keeping to 30 km/h enough?

options.a: Yes, the speed limit alone already covers all necessary caution
options.b: No, you must additionally be ready to brake and expect careless behaviour from children at any time
options.c: No, vehicles may not drive at all in a 30 km/h school zone, only be pushed by hand
options.d: Yes, once a sign is posted, no further duty of care applies

verhalten-39.explanation: A speed sign does not replace the general duty of care towards children - staying ready to brake and paying extra attention are still required on top of it.

verhalten-40.question: You drive past and witness two other vehicles that have just collided. You yourself were not involved in the accident. How do you behave?

options.a: You keep driving, since you were not involved and have no obligations
options.b: Only witnesses with medical training must stop
options.c: You only need to stop if the police are already on scene
options.d: As an uninvolved witness you must provide reasonable assistance, such as calling emergency services or giving first aid

verhalten-40.explanation: Anyone present at an accident is obliged to provide reasonable assistance, regardless of whether they were personally involved. This particularly includes calling emergency services.

autobahn-26.question: You see a round blue sign showing the number 120 on the motorway. What does this sign mean?

options.a: Maximum speed 120 km/h
options.b: Advisory speed of 120 km/h, non-binding recommendation
options.c: Minimum speed of 120 km/h is mandatory
options.d: From here on there is no speed limit

autobahn-26.explanation: Sign 275 (round blue sign) mandates a minimum speed. Anyone unable to maintain it without good reason must not use that lane.

autobahn-27.question: On a three-lane motorway you want to overtake a slower vehicle driving in the middle lane. What is correct?

options.a: You may overtake on the right if the right-hand lane is free
options.b: You may only overtake using the left-hand lane
options.c: You may choose either the left or the right lane to overtake
options.d: Overtaking is generally prohibited on three-lane motorways

autobahn-27.explanation: Overtaking is always done on the left, regardless of how many lanes are available. Overtaking on the right is only permitted in specific slow-moving traffic situations.

autobahn-28.question: Traffic on the motorway has stopped or is only crawling. When must you form an emergency corridor?

options.a: As soon as vehicles are moving at walking pace or standing still
options.b: Only once an emergency vehicle with blue lights is visible
options.c: Only on explicit instruction from the police
options.d: Only if there are more than three lanes per direction

autobahn-28.explanation: An emergency corridor must be formed as soon as traffic on motorways or multi-lane out-of-town roads comes to a crawl or stop, regardless of whether an emergency vehicle is already visible.

autobahn-29.question: At an interchange the hard shoulder is marked as open for use as a running lane during peak hours. How do you behave?

options.a: The hard shoulder may not be used despite being marked open
options.b: You may drive faster there than in the other lanes
options.c: The hard shoulder is only released for buses
options.d: You may use the released hard shoulder like a normal traffic lane

autobahn-29.explanation: A hard shoulder officially released via signage counts as an additional lane and may be used normally for as long as the release is displayed.

autobahn-30.question: You are driving through a motorway construction site with very narrow lanes separated by a solid line. Is overtaking permitted?

options.a: Yes, if the distance to the vehicle ahead is sufficiently large
options.b: No, a solid line must not be crossed
options.c: Yes, but only with hazard lights switched on
options.d: Yes, if no construction vehicles are visible

autobahn-30.explanation: A solid line must never be crossed, not even to overtake. In construction zones this deliberately prevents lane changes.

autobahn-31.question: An electronic gantry display above the motorway shows changing speed values. What applies to you?

options.a: You must comply with whichever speed is currently shown
options.b: The display is only a recommendation with no legal force
options.c: Only the last permanently posted speed limit still applies
options.d: The display only applies to vehicles over 3.5 t

autobahn-31.explanation: Electronic gantry systems display official traffic signs that are just as binding as fixed signs and adapt to the current traffic situation.

autobahn-32.question: You have missed the exit you wanted to take. What do you do?

options.a: Stop immediately on the shoulder and reverse back to the exit
options.b: Turn around via the central reservation if there is no barrier
options.c: Continue to the next exit and leave the motorway there
options.d: Turn around at the right-hand edge of the carriageway if traffic is light

autobahn-32.explanation: Turning around, reversing, and driving against the direction of travel are strictly forbidden on the motorway. If you miss your exit, you must continue to the next one.

autobahn-33.question: The acceleration lane at a motorway on-ramp is unusually short. How do you behave?

options.a: You move onto the through lane and force your way in if necessary
options.b: You stop at the end of the lane and wait for a gap
options.c: You drive significantly faster than the speed limit to merge in sooner
options.d: You adjust your speed to the flowing traffic and use the remaining distance to merge in early

autobahn-33.explanation: On the merge lane, speed must be matched to flowing traffic; stopping on the on-ramp should generally be avoided. If the lane is short, you must watch traffic especially carefully and use a gap early.

autobahn-34.question: While you are overtaking a slower vehicle, it pulls out to the left itself to overtake an even slower vehicle. What is correct?

options.a: You squeeze in between both vehicles to end your overtaking maneuver
options.b: You abort your overtaking maneuver and pull back in behind the vehicle
options.c: You sound the horn and insist on priority since you started overtaking first
options.d: You overtake both vehicles at once by increasing your speed

autobahn-34.explanation: A vehicle being overtaken must not itself speed up or pull out during the maneuver. If it does anyway, the overtaking driver must abandon the overtaking attempt to avoid endangering anyone.

autobahn-35.question: You want to leave the motorway at the next exit. When do you signal?

options.a: In good time, before you move onto the deceleration lane
options.b: Only after you have already reached the deceleration lane
options.c: Signaling is not required when leaving a motorway
options.d: Only shortly before the end of the deceleration lane

autobahn-35.explanation: Every lane change must be signaled in good time so other road users can react to it. This also applies to moving onto the deceleration lane to leave the motorway.

autobahn-36.question: You are driving a long stretch of motorway at night and start feeling drowsy. What is the correct response?

options.a: You briefly open the window and continue driving with loud music
options.b: You drive a bit slower to stay more alert and continue the journey
options.c: You take a break at a suitable rest area before continuing
options.d: You switch on cruise control so you need to concentrate less

autobahn-36.explanation: A drowsy driver is no longer fit to drive. If tiredness sets in, an adequate break at a rest area is necessary before continuing the journey.

autobahn-37.question: Ahead of you, several vehicles' brake lights flash on briefly one after another, though no traffic jam is visible yet. How do you react?

options.a: You ignore it as long as you yourself see no reason to brake
options.b: You ease off the accelerator as a precaution and increase the distance to the vehicle ahead
options.c: You accelerate to get past the suspected jam as quickly as possible
options.d: You immediately move to the far-left lane

autobahn-37.explanation: Brake lights flashing on across several vehicles in sequence are an early warning sign of a traffic disturbance ahead. Anticipatory driving means easing off and gaining distance before the danger becomes visible.

autobahn-38.question: Shortly before the exit to a service area, several vehicles slow down because they want to turn off there. What applies to overtaking in this area?

options.a: Overtaking is generally forbidden there, regardless of the traffic situation
options.b: You may overtake without restriction, since a service area is not a traffic sign
options.c: Overtaking is only permitted if no one is endangered or substantially obstructed, including vehicles turning off
options.d: You must always stop before the service area entrance

autobahn-38.explanation: Overtaking is only allowed if no other road users, including vehicles turning off toward a service area, are endangered or substantially obstructed. Extra caution is required whenever turning traffic is to be expected.

autobahn-39.question: In dense, stop-and-go convoy traffic on the motorway, vehicles in the right-hand lane are sometimes moving faster than those on the left. What applies to so-called lane-hopping ('Kolonnenspringen')?

options.a: Changing to the faster lane is only allowed carefully and with a moderate speed difference, not as a race between lanes
options.b: Changing lanes at all during a traffic jam is generally forbidden
options.c: Drivers may change lanes as often as they like to get ahead faster
options.d: Only vehicles with a trailer may change lanes in convoy traffic

autobahn-39.explanation: In stop-and-go traffic, carefully changing to a faster-moving lane is permitted, but not as reckless, constant lane-hopping with a large speed differential that endangers others.

autobahn-40.question: Traffic radio reports a wrong-way driver on your motorway. What is the best way to react?

options.a: You continue in the left-hand lane, since it offers the best overview
options.b: You accelerate to leave the affected stretch as quickly as possible
options.c: You ignore the report, since wrong-way drivers are usually stopped quickly by police
options.d: You reduce your speed, move to the right-hand lane, and stay prepared for an evasive maneuver

autobahn-40.explanation: When warned about a wrong-way driver, you should reduce speed and use the right-hand lane so you can evade if necessary. Overtaking and unnecessary acceleration increase the risk.

parken-26.question: You are approaching a level crossing marked with a St Andrew's cross sign. May you park just before it?

options.a: Yes, as long as the barriers are open
options.b: No, parking is generally prohibited near level crossings
options.c: Yes, if no train is announced
options.d: Yes, as long as the vehicle stands for less than 5 minutes

parken-26.explanation: Parking is forbidden at level crossings because the view of the tracks and the passage for trains and other vehicles must remain clear.

parken-27.question: You are driving over a narrow bridge where two vehicles can only pass each other with difficulty. May you park there?

options.a: Yes, as long as the handbrake is applied
options.b: Yes, if one lane remains free
options.c: No, parking on narrow bridges is prohibited
options.d: Yes, except in rain

parken-27.explanation: Parking on narrow bridges is generally not allowed, since a parked vehicle would block the already limited space needed for traffic to pass.

parken-28.question: There is a wide driveway shared by several properties. May you park in front of it?

options.a: No, parking in front of driveways is prohibited, even if several properties share it
options.b: Yes, because several residents share the driveway, giving more available space
options.c: Yes, as long as no vehicle is currently entering or exiting
options.d: Yes, if you stay for no more than one hour

parken-28.explanation: Driveways must be kept clear so that authorized users can enter and exit at any time. This applies regardless of how many properties use the driveway.

parken-29.question: How do the distance rules differ between parking near a fire hydrant and near a fire station driveway?

options.a: There is no minimum distance near hydrants, but there is near fire station driveways
options.b: Both areas are subject to exactly the same fixed 10-metre minimum distance
options.c: There is no distance requirement near fire station driveways, but there is near hydrants
options.d: Parking is prohibited near both hydrants and fire station driveways, as its own separate rule for each

parken-29.explanation: Both hydrants and fire station driveways must be kept clear for emergency use. Signage may specify the exact extent, but the basic principle of keeping the area clear applies to both.

parken-30.question: A supplementary sign explicitly permits parking with two wheels on the pavement on a certain street. What applies?

options.a: You may drive fully onto the pavement, since the sign permits any use
options.b: You may only mount the pavement and park to the extent the sign allows, and a strip must remain free for pedestrians
options.c: The sign applies only to motorcycles
options.d: You may park there permanently, i.e. for more than two weeks

parken-30.explanation: Even where pavement parking is permitted, you may only park to the extent indicated, and enough space must always remain for pedestrians.

parken-31.question: You see a sign 'Residents with parking permit No. X exempted' at a parking zone. May you park there without that permit?

options.a: Yes, as long as you stay for no more than 15 minutes
options.b: Yes, if you display a parking disc
options.c: No, without the corresponding resident parking permit you may not park there
options.d: Yes, the rule is generally suspended at night

parken-31.explanation: Resident parking zones are reserved exclusively for holders of the relevant valid permit, regardless of time of day or duration.

parken-32.question: A car park entrance shows a sign giving a maximum height and width. How should you behave?

options.a: Check whether your vehicle, including roof load or attachments, stays within the stated dimensions before entering
options.b: The values only apply to trucks; cars may enter regardless of the values
options.c: The values are non-binding and merely a recommendation
options.d: Only the width matters; the height applies exclusively to buses

parken-32.explanation: Height and width restrictions at car park entrances are binding. Ignoring them risks damage to the vehicle and to the structure.

parken-33.question: You park at night using a parking disc in a zone with a maximum parking duration. What else must you consider?

options.a: The parking disc is no longer required at night
options.b: The arrival time on the disc must still be set correctly despite the darkness, and the vehicle may additionally need parking lights if there is no street lighting
options.c: The disc may be set to any arbitrary time at night
options.d: It is enough to leave the headlights switched on

parken-33.explanation: The obligation to use a parking disc still applies at night. Additionally, outside lit roads, parked vehicles may need to be marked with lights.

parken-34.question: You want to quickly post a letter and leave your parked vehicle's engine running for that. Is this allowed?

options.a: Yes, as long as the vehicle remains locked
options.b: Yes, as long as you are back within three minutes
options.c: No, unnecessary engine noise and avoidable emissions must be avoided, so the engine should be switched off
options.d: Yes, this is explicitly allowed to protect the clutch

parken-34.explanation: Unnecessary noise and avoidable exhaust emissions must generally be avoided. An unattended running engine is also a safety risk.

parken-35.question: Why should you be especially careful when parking near a children's playground?

options.a: Because children can suddenly run out from between vehicles, requiring extra caution
options.b: Because a general no-stopping rule always applies there, regardless of signage
options.c: Because parking there is only allowed with the parents' consent
options.d: Because playgrounds always count as a traffic-calmed zone

parken-35.explanation: Near playgrounds, children may behave unpredictably. Extra caution is therefore required when parking and pulling out.

parken-36.question: Mobile signs in a street announce a no-stopping period for the coming Tuesday due to street cleaning. You park there on Monday. What applies?

options.a: The no-stopping rule already applies from the moment the signs were put up
options.b: As long as the announced period has not started yet, you may park there normally
options.c: Mobile no-stopping signs are legally invalid and may be ignored
options.d: You may only park there with hazard lights on

parken-36.explanation: An announced, time-limited no-stopping order only takes effect from the stated start time. Before that, normal parking is allowed, unless other restrictions apply.

parken-37.question: You are driving a car with a large, heavy trailer. What must you consider when parking that would not matter with a car alone?

options.a: Trailers may generally not be parked anywhere
options.b: No special rule applies; when parking, a trailer is treated as its own separate vehicle and needs no extra space
options.c: The trailer may protrude into the roadway by any amount
options.d: The extra length and weight need more space, and the combination must not block narrow spots like bends

parken-37.explanation: A long, heavy vehicle-trailer combination needs more space to park safely and must not obstruct other traffic, for example at narrow points.

parken-38.question: An area at the roadside is marked with the sign for a taxi rank. May you briefly stop there with your private car to let someone out?

options.a: Yes, this is explicitly allowed as long as no taxi is waiting
options.b: Yes, as long as you stay for more than three minutes
options.c: No, the taxi rank is reserved for taxis and must not be used by other vehicles even to stop
options.d: Yes, but only at night

parken-38.explanation: Taxi ranks are reserved exclusively for taxis. Other vehicles may not stop there, even briefly.

parken-39.question: A parking space at a car park is marked with an electric-vehicle charging symbol and corresponding signage. May you park there with a combustion-engine vehicle?

options.a: Yes, as long as the space happens to be free
options.b: No, such spaces are reserved exclusively for their designated purpose, e.g. electric vehicles while charging
options.c: Yes, as long as you stay no longer than one hour
options.d: Yes, if you display a parking disc

parken-39.explanation: Signed charging spaces are reserved for their specific purpose. Vehicles without a corresponding charging need may not occupy them.

parken-40.question: A sign on private land reads 'Parking for customers only', but nobody enforces it. May you still park there without being entitled to?

options.a: No, the sign reflects the owner's wishes and must be respected even without enforcement; it is unauthorized parking on someone else's property
options.b: Yes, without enforcement the sign has no legal meaning
options.c: Yes, as long as you stay no more than 15 minutes
options.d: Yes, because the StVO generally does not apply on private land, so no rule can be broken

parken-40.explanation: A lack of enforcement does not change the fact that a private parking restriction applies. Parking there anyway is unauthorized and can lead to civil consequences such as towing.

ladung-01.question: Which combination of aids most effectively secures cargo in the boot against shifting?

options.a: Just a light rope around the cargo
options.b: An anti-slip mat combined with lashing straps
options.c: A towel under the cargo
options.d: No aids at all, if the cargo is light

ladung-01.explanation: Anti-slip mats increase friction (force-locking), while lashing straps additionally prevent shifting (form-locking) – combining both is most effective.

ladung-02.question: What must be considered regarding axle load when loading a vehicle?

options.a: Only the total weight matters, distribution is irrelevant
options.b: The load should be placed as far back as possible
options.c: The permitted axle load must not be exceeded on any axle and the vehicle must be loaded in a balanced way
options.d: Only the front axle is relevant

ladung-02.explanation: Even if the total permitted weight is respected, no single axle may be overloaded, as this endangers steering and braking behaviour.

ladung-03.question: What happens if a heavy, unsecured load slides forward during emergency braking?

options.a: It can dangerously strike occupants and affect the vehicle's braking behaviour
options.b: It has no effect on safety in the vehicle
options.c: It automatically shortens the braking distance
options.d: Only the cargo itself can be damaged, nothing else

ladung-03.explanation: A shifting load acts like a projectile and can seriously injure occupants and unpredictably change the vehicle's handling.

ladung-04.question: What determines the maximum permitted load for a roof rack or roof box?

options.a: The driver's personal judgement
options.b: The manufacturer's specified roof load and the vehicle's permitted axle load/total mass
options.c: The size of the roof box, regardless of manufacturer specs
options.d: There is no limit as long as the box is closed

ladung-04.explanation: Both the vehicle manufacturer and the roof rack manufacturer specify maximum roof loads, which must be respected together with the vehicle's permitted total mass.

ladung-05.question: A rear bike rack with bicycles covers the car's number plate light and rear lights. What is required?

options.a: This is fine as long as the bikes are firmly attached
options.b: The car may only be driven during daytime
options.c: An additional, compliant lighting board with number plate and rear lights must be fitted
options.d: The driver must constantly honk to draw attention

ladung-05.explanation: If the number plate or lights are obscured, a separate lighting board with plate, indicators, brake and rear lights must be fitted.

ladung-06.question: What determines which child-seat group is suitable for a child?

options.a: Only the child's age
options.b: Only the number of siblings in the car
options.c: The child's favourite colour
options.d: The child's height and weight, matching the seat's approved category

ladung-06.explanation: Child seats are approved by weight or height, not strictly by age, since children vary in size and weight.

ladung-07.question: From when may a child generally ride in a car without a special child seat, using only the normal seatbelt?

options.a: Once the child is at least 150 cm tall or 12 years old (whichever comes first)
options.b: As soon as the child can walk
options.c: From the 6th birthday, regardless of height
options.d: Never, a child seat is mandatory until adulthood

ladung-07.explanation: The obligation to use a child restraint ends once the child reaches 150 cm in height or turns 12 – whichever happens first.

ladung-08.question: Must pregnant drivers and passengers wear the seatbelt?

options.a: No, pregnant women are generally exempt from the seatbelt requirement
options.b: Yes, the seatbelt obligation generally also applies to pregnant women; the belt should run below the belly
options.c: Only during the first trimester
options.d: Only if a doctor explicitly permits it

ladung-08.explanation: The seatbelt obligation also applies to pregnant women; correct belt positioning below the belly is important to protect the baby in an emergency.

ladung-09.question: What general maximum speed applies in Germany to cars towing a trailer on motorways and expressways, unless a specific exception applies?

options.a: 100 km/h
options.b: 130 km/h
options.c: 80 km/h
options.d: 60 km/h

ladung-09.explanation: Without a special 100 km/h authorisation sticker, cars towing a trailer are generally limited to a maximum of 80 km/h.

ladung-10.question: The trailer is significantly wider than the towing vehicle. What must be taken into account?

options.a: Additional side mirrors giving sufficient view of the trailer's width must be fitted, e.g. wide-angle mirrors
options.b: This is irrelevant as long as one drives carefully
options.c: The trailer may generally no longer be used at all
options.d: Only the interior mirror needs to be adjusted

ladung-10.explanation: If the standard mirrors don't provide a full view of the trailer's width, additional or extended exterior mirrors must be fitted.

ladung-11.question: What belongs to a proper safety check of the trailer coupling before departure?

options.a: Just a quick glance out of the window
options.b: The check is not legally required
options.c: Only checking the trailer's lighting
options.d: Checking that the coupling has latched and is secured, and checking the breakaway/safety cable

ladung-11.explanation: Before every trip with a trailer, it must be checked that the coupling has properly latched and that the safety/breakaway cable is correctly attached.

ladung-12.question: What is the maximum number of people allowed to ride in a car?

options.a: Any number, as long as they hold on well
options.b: Only as many as there are registered seats with seatbelts stated in the vehicle registration
options.c: Always a maximum of four people, regardless of vehicle size
options.d: As many as fit in the boot and on the seats combined

ladung-12.explanation: Only as many people may be transported as there are approved seats with seatbelts listed in the vehicle registration document.

ladung-13.question: How must animals generally be transported in a car?

options.a: Freely moving, so they feel comfortable
options.b: Only on the driver's lap, this calms them
options.c: Secured (e.g. carrier box, harness) so they don't distract the driver and don't become a projectile in a crash
options.d: Animals may generally not be transported in a car at all

ladung-13.explanation: Animals count as cargo and must be secured so they neither distract the driver nor become a hazard during braking.

ladung-14.question: Why shouldn't loose objects like a phone or a water bottle simply lie around freely in the cabin?

options.a: During sudden braking or a crash they can fly through the cabin like projectiles and injure occupants
options.b: It's purely a matter of taste with no safety relevance
options.c: They only make the interior dirty
options.d: They only affect fuel consumption

ladung-14.explanation: Even small, light objects develop significant injury potential during a collision due to deceleration forces.

ladung-15.question: When is a cargo net preferable to securing with lashing straps alone?

options.a: Never, lashing straps are always the better solution
options.b: Only for liquids
options.c: Only for very heavy single items like stone slabs
options.d: For many small or irregularly shaped items, e.g. loose goods in the boot

ladung-15.explanation: Nets are well suited to holding many small or irregular items together over an area, while straps are more sensible for compact, large cargo.

ladung-16.question: An object extends more than 1 metre beyond the rear of the vehicle. What is required?

options.a: Nothing, as long as you drive slowly
options.b: The end of the load must be clearly marked, e.g. with a red warning flag or panel
options.c: This kind of transport is generally prohibited
options.d: It is enough to only drive during daytime

ladung-16.explanation: Cargo that overhangs beyond a certain point must be clearly marked to warn other road users.

ladung-17.question: How should a long ladder be transported in or on the car?

options.a: Loosely hanging out of a window
options.b: Laid unsecured across the back seat
options.c: Firmly lashed in the direction of travel, so it neither shifts nor leaves an unmarked, dangerously protruding end
options.d: It doesn't matter, as long as the boot lid closes

ladung-17.explanation: Long objects must be firmly secured in the direction of travel; any protruding ends must be marked.

ladung-18.question: What should be considered regarding tyre pressure when a vehicle is fully loaded?

options.a: Tyre pressure should be increased according to the manufacturer's specification for the higher load
options.b: Tyre pressure should be reduced to increase the contact area
options.c: Tyre pressure is irrelevant when loading a vehicle
options.d: Tyre pressure may only be adjusted at a tyre change

ladung-18.explanation: Vehicle manufacturers often specify different tyre pressures for partial and full loads to optimise driving safety and tyre wear.

ladung-19.question: Why is the correct nose weight important for a car-caravan combination?

options.a: It only affects fuel consumption
options.b: A nose weight that is too low or too high can lead to dangerous swaying (snaking) of the combination
options.c: It has no influence on driving stability
options.d: It is only relevant for appearance

ladung-19.explanation: Incorrect nose weight destabilises the combination and can lead to dangerous oscillation at higher speeds.

ladung-20.question: Who bears legal responsibility for properly secured cargo?

options.a: Only the registered keeper of the vehicle
options.b: Only the person who loaded the cargo
options.c: No one, as long as no accident happens
options.d: Both the driver and the registered keeper of the vehicle each carry their own duties

ladung-20.explanation: The driver is responsible for ensuring the load is safely secured before departure, while the registered keeper is responsible for the overall organisation of load safety.

ladung-21.question: In simple terms, what is the key difference between force-locking and form-locking load securing?

options.a: Force-locking means the cargo does not need to be secured at all
options.b: Form-locking means only straps may be used
options.c: Force-locking uses friction (e.g. down-lashing), form-locking blocks the cargo directly using fixed barriers such as walls or bracing bars
options.d: Both terms mean the same thing and are interchangeable

ladung-21.explanation: Force-locking securing creates friction through down-lashing, while form-locking uses fixed barriers that physically prevent shifting.

ladung-22.question: A canister of fuel is to be carried privately in the car. What must be taken into account?

options.a: This is generally prohibited, regardless of how it is transported
options.b: The canister must be an approved type, tightly sealed, and secured against tipping over and leaking, ideally separated from the passenger compartment
options.c: It may stand freely in the front passenger's footwell
options.d: It must be carried open during the journey so fumes can escape

ladung-22.explanation: Small quantities of fuel may be carried privately, but only in approved, tightly sealed containers, securely fastened and ideally kept separate from the cabin.

ladung-23.question: What is the maximum permitted total mass of an unbraked trailer generally allowed with a standard Class B driving licence?

options.a: 750 kg

ladung-23.explanation: An unbraked trailer may have a maximum permitted total mass of 750 kg under a standard Class B licence.

ladung-24.question: Why is reversing with a trailer particularly demanding?

options.a: Because it is generally prohibited by law
options.b: Because speed must be higher than usual while doing it
options.c: Because rearward visibility is often limited and the trailer moves opposite to the steering input
options.d: Because mirrors may not be used during this manoeuvre

ladung-24.explanation: When reversing with a trailer, it moves opposite to the steering input, which together with limited visibility requires high attention, ideally with a spotter.

ladung-25.question: What should be checked regarding exterior mirrors before a trip with a wide trailer?

options.a: Only whether the mirrors are clean, that is enough
options.b: Nothing, standard mirrors are always sufficient
options.c: Whether the mirrors can be removed to reduce wind resistance
options.d: Whether the mirrors give sufficient all-round view of the trailer, fitting trailer wide-angle mirrors if necessary

ladung-25.explanation: If the standard view is insufficient, additional trailer wide-angle mirrors must be fitted to fully see the trailer.

ladung-26.question: When should load securing be checked?

options.a: Only once, before the very first trip with the vehicle
options.b: Before departure and again during breaks on longer journeys
options.c: Only if the police ask about it
options.d: Checking is not necessary if the load was firm when loaded

ladung-26.explanation: Cargo can loosen during the journey, so it should be checked before departure and again during breaks on longer trips.

ladung-27.question: What danger arises specifically during emergency braking due to inadequately secured cargo?

options.a: The cargo can be catapulted forward and hit occupants or the windscreen
options.b: There is no additional danger at all
options.c: The brakes automatically fail as a result
options.d: Only the tyres can be damaged

ladung-27.explanation: During emergency braking, enormous deceleration forces act, which can hurl unsecured cargo forward.

ladung-28.question: How should a dog be correctly secured in a car?

options.a: It may roam freely in the vehicle, as long as it behaves
options.b: It should ride on the driver's lap
options.c: With a suitable safety harness, in a secured carrier box, or behind a sturdy dog guard in the boot
options.d: A dog does not need to be secured because it can hold on by itself

ladung-28.explanation: An unsecured dog can become a projectile during braking and distract the driver; a harness, box or dog guard prevents this.

ladung-29.question: What effect do roof boxes or roof racks typically have on fuel consumption and driving noise?

options.a: They reduce consumption because they improve aerodynamics
options.b: Due to the additional air resistance, they usually increase fuel consumption and wind noise
options.c: They have no effect whatsoever on consumption or noise
options.d: They reduce wind noise but do not increase consumption

ladung-29.explanation: Roof attachments significantly increase air resistance, leading to noticeably higher fuel consumption and more wind noise.

ladung-30.question: Can someone be exempted from the seatbelt obligation?

options.a: No, the seatbelt obligation applies to everyone without exception
options.b: Yes, anyone can simply exempt themselves if they find the belt uncomfortable
options.c: Only children under 3 are generally exempt, no one else
options.d: Yes, in justified medical exceptional cases a doctor-certified exemption from the seatbelt obligation may apply

ladung-30.explanation: In justified medical exceptional cases, a doctor-certified exemption from the seatbelt obligation is possible.

ladung-31.question: While driving, you notice that cargo in the boot is audibly moving and shifting. What is correct?

options.a: Continue driving, as long as you can't see it
options.b: Stop safely at the next opportunity and re-secure the load
options.c: Turn up the radio so you no longer hear it
options.d: Increase speed so the load sits more stably due to centrifugal force

ladung-31.explanation: Shifting cargo is an acute safety risk and must be re-secured at the next safe opportunity.

ladung-32.question: What is the purpose of corner protectors when lashing cargo with straps?

options.a: They only increase the tensile strength of the strap
options.b: They are purely decorative with no technical purpose
options.c: They protect the strap from the cargo's sharp edges and prevent the strap from chafing through or tearing
options.d: They make additional straps unnecessary

ladung-32.explanation: Corner protectors prevent sharp edges of the cargo from damaging the strap, which could otherwise cause the strap to tear.

ladung-33.question: Why is it important to know the total height of a loaded vehicle before entering a car park or driving under a low bridge?

options.a: Because excessive load height can collide with bridges, tunnels or car park barriers, causing serious damage or accidents
options.b: Because otherwise the tyres will burst
options.c: Because this is only relevant for trucks, not cars with roof loads
options.d: Because height has no relevance to the journey at all

ladung-33.explanation: A roof box or tall load changes the vehicle's total height, which must absolutely be taken into account regarding clearance heights.

ladung-34.question: A taxi has no suitable child seat available. What applies to transporting a small child?

options.a: The child may always ride without any restraint whatsoever, simply because it is a taxi
options.b: The child restraint rule also applies in taxis; without a child seat, a child may only ride in narrow exceptional cases, such as a short emergency trip
options.c: Taxis are completely exempt from the seatbelt requirement for children
options.d: The child must sit on an adult's lap without a belt

ladung-34.explanation: The obligation for age-appropriate child restraint generally also applies in taxis; only in narrow legal exceptional cases may the journey be made without a child seat.

ladung-35.question: What general duty exists regarding cargo and the visibility of number plates, lighting and mirrors?

options.a: Cargo may be placed anywhere, as long as it stays inside the vehicle
options.b: Only the windscreen must stay clear, everything else is irrelevant
options.c: The cargo must not obscure or impair the number plate, lighting devices, or the driver's visibility
options.d: This duty applies only to commercial vehicles

ladung-35.explanation: Cargo must not impair the driver's view, the number plate, or the lighting, as this endangers other road users.

ladung-36.question: What is the most sensible way to transport loose shopping bags in the boot?

options.a: In a sturdy box or secured with a net/strap, so they don't fly around during corners or braking
options.b: Loosely spread out, so they take up more space
options.c: On the back seat with no securing at all, that's enough
options.d: It doesn't matter, since shopping bags are too light to become dangerous

ladung-36.explanation: Even light loose items can fly around during hard braking or cornering and should therefore be secured in boxes or with nets.

ladung-37.question: How does the braking behaviour of a car-trailer combination change compared to the vehicle alone?

options.a: The braking distance shortens, because the trailer brakes as well
options.b: There is no difference in braking behaviour at all
options.c: Only unbraked trailers change anything, braked trailers never do
options.d: The braking distance generally increases due to the additional mass, especially noticeable with unbraked trailers

ladung-37.explanation: The additional mass of a trailer generally increases the braking distance, which is especially important to consider with unbraked trailers.

ladung-38.question: A mattress is to be transported on the car roof. What is especially important?

options.a: Only that the mattress lies in the middle of the roof
options.b: Firm lashing with several straps lengthwise and crosswise, and checking that nothing loosens during the journey
options.c: It is enough to hold the mattress out of the window by hand
options.d: Securing is not necessary for mattresses since they are very light

ladung-38.explanation: Large, light objects like mattresses can come loose in the wind and must therefore be firmly lashed crosswise with several straps.

ladung-39.question: Cargo protrudes sideways beyond the width of the vehicle. What generally applies here?

options.a: This is generally allowed without any restriction
options.b: Sideways overhang is always prohibited, regardless of extent
options.c: A small sideways overhang may be permitted, but must be clearly marked in darkness/poor visibility
options.d: Sideways overhang is only relevant for trailers, never for the car itself

ladung-39.explanation: A small sideways overhang may be permitted, but it must be clearly marked, especially in darkness, to warn other road users.

ladung-40.question: What is the fundamental legal requirement for any cargo, regardless of the type of goods being transported?

options.a: The cargo must be stowed and secured so that it cannot shift, tip over, or fall off even during emergency braking, sudden evasive action, or on uneven road surfaces
options.b: The cargo only needs to be secured at speeds above 100 km/h
options.c: It is sufficient if the cargo is not visible
options.d: Securing is only required for commercial transports

ladung-40.explanation: §22 Abs. 1 StVO requires that cargo is stowed so that it cannot shift even under normal driving conditions such as braking or evasive manoeuvres.

erstehilfe-01.question: You are the first to arrive at a fresh accident scene. What should you do first?

options.a: Run to the injured immediately
options.b: Secure the scene (hazard lights, warning vest, warning triangle)
options.c: Take photos for insurance
options.d: Wait for the police without doing anything

erstehilfe-01.explanation: Before helping, the scene must be secured so no further people get injured.

erstehilfe-02.question: At roughly what distance should you place the warning triangle before an accident on a rural road?

options.a: About 10 meters
options.b: About 50 meters
options.c: About 100 meters
options.d: About 400 meters

erstehilfe-02.explanation: On rural roads a rough guideline of about 100 meters gives following traffic enough time to react.

erstehilfe-03.question: Before which type of stretch should the warning triangle be placed noticeably farther than the usual ~100 meters?

options.a: A straight, clear stretch
options.b: A 30 km/h zone
options.c: Directly before a traffic light
options.d: A blind curve or hillcrest

erstehilfe-03.explanation: Before curves or hillcrests, drivers need more time to spot the danger, so the distance is increased (often 150-400 meters on motorways).

erstehilfe-04.question: What should you do immediately once you have stopped your vehicle after a crash?

options.a: Switch on the hazard warning lights
options.b: Leave the engine running unnecessarily
options.c: Turn the music up
options.d: Drive off immediately to make room

erstehilfe-04.explanation: Hazard lights immediately alert other road users to the danger spot.

erstehilfe-05.question: At night on a rural road you need to get out to secure the scene. What is correct?

options.a: Look for the warning vest in the trunk only after getting out
options.b: Put the warning vest on inside the vehicle before getting out, if possible
options.c: Skip the vest if you are in a hurry
options.d: Only give the vest to the passenger

erstehilfe-05.explanation: Anyone who needs to be visible outside the vehicle should put the vest on before stepping out, so they are not overlooked themselves.

erstehilfe-06.question: You approach a badly damaged crashed vehicle from which liquid is leaking. How do you behave?

options.a: Light a cigarette to calm down
options.b: Check with a lighter whether it is fuel
options.c: Avoid open flames and smoking, and approach carefully
options.d: Honk loudly to wake the occupants

erstehilfe-06.explanation: Leaking liquid could be fuel; open flames or sparks could start a fire.

erstehilfe-07.question: When is an unconscious person placed in the recovery position?

options.a: When they are responsive
options.b: When they are unconscious but breathing normally
options.c: When they are not breathing
options.d: Only when a doctor orders it

erstehilfe-07.explanation: The recovery position protects the airway of an unconscious but breathing person from being blocked, e.g. by vomit or the tongue.

erstehilfe-08.question: How do you first check whether an unresponsive person is conscious?

options.a: Speak loudly to them and gently shake their shoulders
options.b: Start chest compressions immediately
options.c: Pour cold water on their face
options.d: Wait until the person reacts on their own

erstehilfe-08.explanation: Speaking to and gently shaking the person is the recognised way to check consciousness without causing further injury.

erstehilfe-09.question: A person is unresponsive. You have opened the airway by tilting the head back. How do you check breathing?

options.a: Feel the pulse at the wrist
options.b: Ask if the person is breathing
options.c: Press on the chest
options.d: Look, listen, and feel for chest movement and airflow

erstehilfe-09.explanation: Looking, listening, and feeling for about 10 seconds reliably shows whether a person is breathing normally.

erstehilfe-10.question: Which telephone number do you dial in Germany to alert the emergency medical service and fire brigade?
erstehilfe-10.explanation: 112 is the Europe-wide emergency number for ambulance and fire services and can be reached even without credit or your own provider's coverage.

erstehilfe-11.question: Which details are part of the classic 'W-questions' when making an emergency call?

options.a: Weather, car colour, preferred hospital, travel time
options.b: Caller's name, age, birthplace, birthday
options.c: Where it happened, what happened, how many injured, what injuries, wait for questions
options.d: Car model, car age, garage, service history

erstehilfe-11.explanation: These five points give the dispatch centre all the key information needed to send the right help.

erstehilfe-12.question: You drive past an accident where help is clearly needed and simply continue on. What legal consequence can this have?

options.a: Criminal liability for failure to render assistance
options.b: None, since you did not cause the accident
options.c: Only a fine like for illegal parking
options.d: Only a warning at the next vehicle inspection

erstehilfe-12.explanation: Under §323c StGB, everyone is obliged to provide reasonable help in an emergency, regardless of whether they were involved in causing it.

erstehilfe-13.question: A burning vehicle blocks the road and you are not a first responder. How far does your duty to help extend?

options.a: You must enter the burning vehicle even at serious risk to yourself
options.b: You must help as far as is reasonable without serious risk to yourself, e.g. call emergency services
options.c: You have no duty at all since you are not a firefighter
options.d: You may only help if the police allow it

erstehilfe-13.explanation: The duty to help ends where it would create serious risk to yourself; making an emergency call is almost always reasonable, though.

erstehilfe-14.question: You are not involved in the accident but pass by as a witness, and sufficient competent help is already on scene. How do you behave?

options.a: You may continue driving if genuinely enough help is present and no one else is needed
options.b: You must still stop and provide first aid yourself
options.c: You must call the police even if someone already has
options.d: You may under no circumstances continue driving

erstehilfe-14.explanation: The duty to help applies as long as help is actually needed; if enough help is already present, you do not need to intervene as well.

erstehilfe-15.question: An injured motorcyclist lies unconscious on the road and it is not clearly visible whether they are breathing. What do you do about the helmet?

options.a: Never remove the helmet under any circumstances
options.b: Only remove the helmet if the police order it
options.c: Carefully remove the helmet, ideally with two people, to check and secure breathing and consciousness
options.d: Cut the helmet open with a sharp object

erstehilfe-15.explanation: If breathing or consciousness cannot be reliably assessed, the helmet must be carefully removed, ideally by two helpers to protect the neck.

erstehilfe-16.question: How do you stop a heavily bleeding wound on a leg while waiting for the ambulance?

options.a: Rinse the wound generously with water and leave it open
options.b: Apply firm, direct pressure to the wound with a dressing or clean cloth
options.c: Just watch until professionals arrive
options.d: Ask the injured person to walk around to stimulate circulation

erstehilfe-16.explanation: Direct pressure on the wound is the most effective immediate measure to reduce heavy blood loss.

erstehilfe-17.question: An accident victim is pale, has cold sweat, and a rapid pulse, with no visible leg or head injuries. What do you suspect and what do you do?

options.a: Shock; elevate the legs and keep the person warm
options.b: Nausea; give them something to eat right away
options.c: That they are pretending; ignore them
options.d: A cold; open a window

erstehilfe-17.explanation: Paleness, cold sweat, and a rapid pulse are typical signs of shock; elevating the legs and keeping the person warm supports blood flow to vital organs.

erstehilfe-18.question: In which case should you NOT elevate the legs of a person in shock?

options.a: A minor graze on the arm
options.b: A bruise on the hand
options.c: Nausea with no visible injury
options.d: A suspected broken leg or a serious head or spine injury

erstehilfe-18.explanation: If a leg, head, or spine injury is suspected, elevating the legs could worsen the injury, so it should be avoided.

erstehilfe-19.question: Your vehicle stops behind a burning crashed car. How do you behave regarding the people in the burning vehicle?

options.a: Open the bonnet to put the fire out yourself
options.b: Wait until the car has burned out
options.c: Move people out of the immediate danger zone to a safe distance if this is possible without major risk to yourself
options.d: Smash the windows no matter what the situation looks like

erstehilfe-19.explanation: Moving people out of the immediate danger zone of a vehicle fire is a priority, provided it is possible without disproportionate risk to yourself.

erstehilfe-20.question: In which situation must you always call the police after a road accident?

options.a: A tiny paint scratch that both sides immediately accept
options.b: When people are injured or fault is disputed
options.c: When both vehicles are the same colour
options.d: Only if it is raining

erstehilfe-20.explanation: In case of injuries or an unclear question of fault, the police must be involved to officially establish the facts.

erstehilfe-21.question: For minor sheet-metal damage with no injuries, where both drivers agree, what is sufficient?

options.a: Exchange names, addresses, and insurance details and document the accident if needed
options.b: Drive off immediately without any further exchange
options.c: Always call the fire brigade
options.d: Swap vehicles

erstehilfe-21.explanation: For undisputed minor damage, exchanging the necessary details is usually sufficient without needing to involve the police.

erstehilfe-22.question: What must a first-aid kit in a car basically contain according to current requirements?

options.a: Only plasters
options.b: Only a flashlight
options.c: Repair tools
options.d: Standardised dressing material such as wound dressings, bandages, plasters, and gloves

erstehilfe-22.explanation: The first-aid kit must contain DIN-standardised material sufficient for the initial treatment of injuries.

erstehilfe-23.question: Why should you regularly check the expiry date on your first-aid kit?

options.a: Expired kits are more expensive to buy
options.b: Otherwise the vehicle inspection seal becomes invalid
options.c: Sterile material can lose its protective effect after expiry and should be replaced
options.d: The expiry date has no meaning at all

erstehilfe-23.explanation: Expired dressing material can be non-sterile or brittle and should be replaced so it works properly in an emergency.

erstehilfe-24.question: At an accident scene a child is injured and the parents are present but distraught. How do you behave?

options.a: Ignore the child, since children would need to be treated completely differently from adults
options.b: Stay calm, provide first aid to the child following the usual principles, and involve the parents where possible
options.c: Immediately hand full responsibility to the parents and do nothing yourself
options.d: Wait until the child gives information on its own

erstehilfe-24.explanation: A calm, reassuring manner helps calm the child; the basic first-aid principles apply essentially the same as for adults.

erstehilfe-25.question: An unconscious but normally breathing person is lying on their back. What matters most for the airway?

options.a: Tilt the head back and/or place the person in the recovery position to keep the airway clear
options.b: Give the person water to drink
options.c: Lay the person face-down on their stomach
options.d: Do nothing until the ambulance arrives

erstehilfe-25.explanation: A clear airway is vital; the recovery position prevents the tongue or vomit from blocking breathing.

erstehilfe-26.question: Near an accident there is a damaged truck displaying an orange hazard placard for dangerous-goods transport. How do you behave?

options.a: Approach as closely as possible to help
options.b: Keep a clear safety distance, avoid open flames, and note the placard's markings for the emergency call
options.c: Inspect the cargo yourself
options.d: Remove the placard so no one misunderstands it

erstehilfe-26.explanation: Hazardous-materials accidents can carry extra risks such as toxic substances or explosion danger; keeping distance and reporting the markings to the dispatch centre is essential.

erstehilfe-27.question: After an accident on the motorway you have to wait for help on the hard shoulder. Where should you stay?

options.a: Right next to your vehicle on the hard shoulder
options.b: On the carriageway to give signals
options.c: Behind the guardrail or at a safe distance outside the carriageway
options.d: Inside the vehicle with the seatbelt fastened

erstehilfe-27.explanation: The area behind the guardrail offers the best protection from following traffic that might swerve onto the hard shoulder.

erstehilfe-28.question: In darkness, besides the warning triangle, what additional aid helps draw attention to the danger spot?

options.a: Hazard lights and, if needed, a flashlight or phone light to wave
options.b: A loud car radio
options.c: Your vehicle's high beams pointed directly at oncoming traffic
options.d: Nothing additional

erstehilfe-28.explanation: Additional visible signals such as a flashlight significantly improve the visibility of the danger spot in the dark.

erstehilfe-29.question: An injured person complains of severe back pain and a possible spinal injury after an accident. How do you behave as long as there is no acute danger?

options.a: Sit the person up immediately so they can breathe better
options.b: Roll the person to the side to see the wound
options.c: Ask the person to stand up to make room
options.d: Avoid moving the person if possible and reassure them until professionals arrive

erstehilfe-29.explanation: Unnecessary movement can worsen a spinal injury; the person should only be moved in case of immediate danger (e.g. fire).

erstehilfe-30.question: You are a layperson providing first aid. How do you handle measures beyond your knowledge, e.g. removing an object deeply embedded in a wound?

options.a: Confidently pull the object out yourself
options.b: Refrain from such measures and leave the object in place as far as possible until professionals arrive
options.c: Push the object in deeper
options.d: Wait without helping at all

erstehilfe-30.explanation: Lay helpers should only carry out measures they are confident in; removing embedded objects can cause heavier bleeding.

erstehilfe-31.question: At an accident with several injured people of differing severity, how do you generally proceed as a first aider?

options.a: Always help whoever is screaming loudest first
options.b: Always help whoever is closest first
options.c: First attend to the person who is most severely, life-threateningly injured
options.d: Treat everyone at the same time

erstehilfe-31.explanation: Loud screaming is often a sign that breathing is intact, while quiet, motionless people often need the most urgent help.

erstehilfe-32.question: As a witness you see another driver simply drive off after a damage-only accident without giving their details. What should you do?

options.a: Nothing, it is none of your business
options.b: Note the number plate and vehicle features and inform the police
options.c: Chase the vehicle yourself and stop it
options.d: Post about it on social media instead of calling the police

erstehilfe-32.explanation: Noting the number plate and vehicle features helps the police trace the driver who fled the scene without authorisation.

erstehilfe-33.question: For an accident with property damage, what is especially helpful for later insurance settlement?

options.a: Photos of the final positions, the damage, and the scene, plus exchanging contact and insurance details
options.b: Cleaning the vehicles immediately
options.c: Giving no details and simply driving off
options.d: Only verbal assurances without documentation

erstehilfe-33.explanation: Photos and exchanged details serve as evidence and make it easier to clarify fault later.

erstehilfe-34.question: Your own vehicle starts smoking and catches fire while driving. How do you behave?

options.a: Keep driving to the nearest garage
options.b: Open the bonnet immediately while still driving
options.c: Stop as safely as possible, well clear of the carriageway, get all occupants out and away from the vehicle, then call for help
options.d: Close the windows to keep smoke out and stay seated in the car

erstehilfe-34.explanation: Stopping safely and quickly leaving the vehicle is the top priority, since a burning vehicle can develop rapidly.

erstehilfe-35.question: How far does the general duty to help extend for a layperson at an accident scene?

options.a: You must perform medical procedures like injections yourself
options.b: You must do what is reasonable and possible for a layperson, e.g. call for help, secure the scene, basic first aid
options.c: You must take over full medical care until the ambulance arrives
options.d: There is no duty at all unless a doctor is present

erstehilfe-35.explanation: Laypeople are only expected to provide reasonable help matching their knowledge, not professional medical treatment.

erstehilfe-36.question: Does the first-aid course certificate (immediate measures at the scene of an accident) submitted when getting your licence need to be renewed regularly to keep the licence valid?

options.a: At most 6 months old
options.b: At most 1 year old
options.c: There is no fixed statutory expiry, the certificate generally remains valid for the licence
options.d: It must be retaken every year to keep the licence

erstehilfe-36.explanation: The certificate for the immediate-measures course is required once to obtain the licence and does not automatically expire for that purpose, though refreshing the knowledge regularly is still recommended.

erstehilfe-37.question: You need to get out after an accident on a multi-lane road at night. What is the most sensible order of steps?

options.a: Park the vehicle safely, switch on hazard lights, put on the warning vest, then get out
options.b: Get out immediately and look for the vest afterwards
options.c: Photograph the scene first, then get out
options.d: Get out and stand in the middle of the carriageway to watch traffic

erstehilfe-37.explanation: This order ensures you are already visible and protected before stepping into moving traffic.

erstehilfe-38.question: You are giving first aid alone to an unconscious, breathing person and waiting for the ambulance. What is important?

options.a: Leave the person alone if possible and wait inside your vehicle
options.b: Check breathing only once at the start and not again afterwards
options.c: Wake the person up so they do not stay unconscious
options.d: Keep checking breathing regularly until professional help arrives

erstehilfe-38.explanation: The condition can change; regularly checking breathing ensures you can react in time if it deteriorates.

erstehilfe-39.question: Does the duty to help and provide information at an accident apply only to the person who caused it?

options.a: Yes, only the person at fault has duties
options.b: No, everyone directly involved in the accident generally has duties to cooperate, regardless of fault
options.c: No, only if the damage exceeds 5,000 euros
options.d: Yes, but only for accidents on motorways

erstehilfe-39.explanation: The duties after an accident, such as providing personal details, apply to everyone involved, not only to the person who caused it.

erstehilfe-40.question: After an accident, a vehicle occupant is conscious but trapped in the deformed vehicle, with no acute fire or explosion risk. How do you behave?

options.a: Forcefully pull the person out of the vehicle yourself
options.b: Do nothing and just wait, without reassuring the person
options.c: Reassure and look after the person, and without acute danger do not attempt to free them yourself but wait for professional rescue
options.d: Forcibly pry the door open with a tool

erstehilfe-40.explanation: Without immediate danger, technical extrication should be left to professionals to avoid causing additional injuries during the rescue.

fahrtuechtigkeit-01.question: From which blood alcohol level does the 0.5 per mille limit apply as an administrative offence for experienced drivers?

options.a: From 0.3 per mille
options.b: From 0.5 per mille
options.c: From 0.8 per mille
options.d: From 1.1 per mille

fahrtuechtigkeit-01.explanation: From 0.5 per mille it is an administrative offence with a fine, points, and usually a driving ban.

fahrtuechtigkeit-02.question: From which blood alcohol level is a driver considered absolutely unfit to drive, treated as a criminal offence regardless of driving behaviour?

options.a: From 0.5 per mille
options.b: From 0.8 per mille
options.c: From 1.1 per mille
options.d: From 1.6 per mille

fahrtuechtigkeit-02.explanation: From 1.1 per mille a driver is considered absolutely unfit to drive; this is a criminal offence under §316 StGB, even without noticeably erratic driving.

fahrtuechtigkeit-03.question: What blood alcohol limit applies during the probationary period and for novice drivers under 21?

options.a: 0.0 per mille
options.b: 0.3 per mille
options.c: 0.5 per mille
options.d: 0.8 per mille

fahrtuechtigkeit-03.explanation: For novice drivers in the probationary period and all drivers under 21, an absolute alcohol ban applies while driving.

fahrtuechtigkeit-04.question: What does the so-called 0.3 per mille threshold mean in German case law?

options.a: The licence is automatically revoked from this level
options.b: Already from 0.3 per mille it can be treated as a criminal offence if driving errors or an accident also occur
options.c: Driving is generally forbidden from 0.3 per mille
options.d: This value only applies to cyclists

fahrtuechtigkeit-04.explanation: Under so-called relative unfitness to drive, alcohol-related driving errors or an accident from around 0.3 per mille onward can already lead to criminal liability.

fahrtuechtigkeit-05.question: What is a typical consequence of a first-time offence with 0.6 per mille while driving?

options.a: A fine, points in Flensburg, and usually a driving ban
options.b: Only a verbal warning with no further consequences
options.c: Immediate and permanent revocation of the driving licence
options.d: Imprisonment without probation

fahrtuechtigkeit-05.explanation: In the administrative-offence range (0.5 up to just under 1.1 per mille), a fine, points, and usually a temporary driving ban are the consequence.

fahrtuechtigkeit-06.question: Roughly how does the body break down alcohol in the blood?

options.a: Completely within a few minutes
options.b: Breakdown depends solely on body weight and is exactly the same speed for everyone
options.c: Alcohol is not broken down at all, only sweated out
options.d: Only slowly over several hours, with the exact speed varying from person to person

fahrtuechtigkeit-06.explanation: Breaking down alcohol takes several hours and the exact speed varies between individuals - it cannot be sped up.

fahrtuechtigkeit-07.question: Is it true that a strong coffee quickly lowers your blood alcohol level and makes you fit to drive again?

options.a: Yes, caffeine chemically breaks down alcohol
options.b: Yes, but only with caffeinated energy drinks, not coffee
options.c: No, coffee may make you feel more alert but does not lower the alcohol level in your blood
options.d: Yes, if combined with a cold shower

fahrtuechtigkeit-07.explanation: Coffee, a cold shower, or fresh air do not change your blood alcohol level - only time breaks alcohol down.

fahrtuechtigkeit-08.question: What rule generally applies to driving after using illegal drugs such as cocaine or certain other substances?

options.a: A generous tolerance limit applies, similar to alcohol
options.b: A zero-tolerance approach generally applies once a measurable substance is found in the blood
options.c: Drug use while driving is only relevant if an accident occurs
options.d: Only novice drivers are banned, experienced drivers may use drugs

fahrtuechtigkeit-08.explanation: For many illegal substances, a zero-tolerance approach generally applies: even a trace found in the blood can be enough for a fine or a criminal charge.

fahrtuechtigkeit-09.question: Why should you check the package leaflet of an over-the-counter medication like an antihistamine before driving?

options.a: Because such medication can cause drowsiness and impair fitness to drive
options.b: Because over-the-counter medication is generally forbidden
options.c: Because the leaflet changes the legal blood alcohol limit
options.d: The leaflet has no relevance to fitness to drive

fahrtuechtigkeit-09.explanation: Many over-the-counter medications, for example for allergies or colds, can cause drowsiness; the leaflet usually warns explicitly about impaired fitness to drive.

fahrtuechtigkeit-10.question: What applies to prescription sedatives in road traffic?

options.a: They are allowed as long as a prescription exists, regardless of their effect
options.b: They are generally harmless because a doctor prescribed them
options.c: They can significantly impair fitness to drive, even when prescribed by a doctor
options.d: They only affect pedestrians, not drivers

fahrtuechtigkeit-10.explanation: Even medication prescribed by a doctor can severely reduce reaction ability; drivers themselves are responsible for checking their own fitness to drive.

fahrtuechtigkeit-11.question: Why is the combination of alcohol and tiredness particularly dangerous?

options.a: Because alcohol fully compensates for tiredness
options.b: Because the two effects reinforce each other and further worsen reaction time and concentration
options.c: Because tiredness speeds up alcohol breakdown
options.d: The combination has no additional effect

fahrtuechtigkeit-11.explanation: Tiredness and alcohol reinforce each other and lead to significantly longer reaction times and worse concentration.

fahrtuechtigkeit-12.question: What can legally happen if you refuse a voluntary breath alcohol test during a police check?

options.a: If there is reasonable suspicion, the police can order further measures such as a blood test
options.b: Refusing always has no consequences at all, since the test is voluntary
options.c: Refusal automatically leads to imprisonment
options.d: The police are then not allowed to take any further steps

fahrtuechtigkeit-12.explanation: The breath test itself is usually voluntary, but if there is reasonable suspicion the police can order a blood test, which cannot be refused.

fahrtuechtigkeit-13.question: What typically happens during a traffic check if the police notice signs of impairment from alcohol or drugs?

options.a: The driver is released immediately without any further check
options.b: This is usually followed by a preliminary test and, if applicable, an ordered blood test for accurate determination
options.c: The licence is permanently confiscated on the spot without any further examination
options.d: Only the vehicle is seized

fahrtuechtigkeit-13.explanation: If there is suspicion, this is usually followed by a preliminary test (e.g. breath test or rapid drug test), and if suspicion is confirmed a blood test can be ordered.

fahrtuechtigkeit-14.question: When can the medical-psychological assessment (MPU, colloquially called the 'idiot test') be ordered by the licensing authority?

options.a: For every minor administrative traffic offence
options.b: Only when applying for a licence for the first time, regardless of any incidents
options.c: For example after a high blood alcohol reading, repeated alcohol or drug offences, or doubts about fitness to drive
options.d: Never, the MPU was abolished in Germany

fahrtuechtigkeit-14.explanation: The MPU is ordered, among other cases, after a high blood alcohol reading (e.g. from 1.6 per mille), repeated offences, or other doubts about fitness to drive, in order to assess driving fitness.

fahrtuechtigkeit-15.question: What does the MPU roughly assess?

options.a: Only driving skills on a fixed test track
options.b: Personal fitness, such as insight into one's own behaviour and the likelihood of reoffending
options.c: Only physical fitness, with no psychological aspects
options.d: Only theoretical traffic knowledge, like the standard theory exam

fahrtuechtigkeit-15.explanation: The MPU examines medical and psychological aspects of fitness to drive, including whether a change in behaviour has taken place.

fahrtuechtigkeit-16.question: How does licence revocation fundamentally differ from a driving ban?

options.a: With revocation, the licence is fully cancelled and must be newly applied for, whereas with a driving ban it remains valid but cannot be used for a limited time
options.b: Legally there is no difference between the two terms
options.c: A driving ban is always permanent, revocation only temporary
options.d: Revocation only applies to motorcycles, the driving ban only to cars

fahrtuechtigkeit-16.explanation: A driving ban is a time-limited suspension of use while the licence itself remains valid, while revocation cancels the licence entirely and requires it to be newly obtained.

fahrtuechtigkeit-17.question: What is a typical consequence of repeated alcohol-related traffic offences?

options.a: Sanctions generally become milder with each further offence
options.b: There is generally no escalation, every offence is treated the same
options.c: Only the very first offence carries any consequences at all
options.d: Consequences usually escalate, for example through higher fines, longer driving bans, or licence revocation

fahrtuechtigkeit-17.explanation: Repeat offenders must expect considerably stricter sanctions, up to permanent licence revocation and an ordered MPU.

fahrtuechtigkeit-18.question: Does a blood alcohol limit also apply to cycling?

options.a: No, there is no alcohol regulation for bicycles at all
options.b: Yes, however the threshold for absolute unfitness to ride is higher for bicycles than for cars
options.c: Yes, exactly the same 0.5 per mille limit as for cars applies
options.d: Yes, but only for e-bikes, not for regular bicycles

fahrtuechtigkeit-18.explanation: Cyclists can also be held criminally liable; the threshold for absolute unfitness is higher for bicycles than for cars, but it should still be taken seriously.

fahrtuechtigkeit-19.question: How are e-scooters treated regarding drink-driving rules?

options.a: Basically the same blood alcohol limits apply as for car drivers
options.b: There are no alcohol rules at all for e-scooters
options.c: The same, considerably more relaxed rules apply as for bicycles
options.d: Alcohol is legally irrelevant for e-scooters because they are considered toys

fahrtuechtigkeit-19.explanation: E-scooters are legally classified as motor vehicles, so the same blood alcohol limits as for cars apply - including criminal liability from 1.1 per mille.

fahrtuechtigkeit-20.question: What is meant by 'Restalkohol' (residual alcohol)?

options.a: Alcohol that was spilled while drinking
options.b: A special type of non-alcoholic drink
options.c: Alcohol that is still detectable in the blood the morning after drinking and can impair fitness to drive
options.d: A technical term for the maximum legal blood alcohol limit

fahrtuechtigkeit-20.explanation: Residual alcohol can still be measurable hours after the last drink and can unexpectedly put you over the legal limit the next morning.

fahrtuechtigkeit-21.question: What can be a possible consequence of an alcohol-related offence during the probationary period for the period itself?

options.a: The probationary period is automatically shortened
options.b: The probationary period is unrelated to such offences
options.c: The probationary period ends immediately and the licence becomes permanent
options.d: The probationary period can be extended, in addition to other measures such as a remedial seminar

fahrtuechtigkeit-21.explanation: For a serious offence, such as breaching the alcohol ban during the probationary period, the licensing authority can extend the probationary period and order a remedial seminar.

fahrtuechtigkeit-22.question: What consequence can an alcohol-related traffic accident have for insurance cover?

options.a: The insurer always covers the full damage without limitation
options.b: The vehicle insurer can seek reimbursement (Regress) from the driver in cases of gross negligence such as drink-driving
options.c: Insurers are generally not allowed to pay at all if alcohol was involved
options.d: Alcohol is legally irrelevant to insurance
